units.zh: 成汭，淮西人。
units.en: Cheng Rui came from west of the Huai.
units.literal: Cheng Rui was a native of Huai West.

units.zh: 少年任俠，乘醉殺人，為仇家所捕，因落發為僧，冒姓郭氏。
units.en: As a young man he killed someone in a drunken brawl, was hunted by the victim's kin, shaved his head as a monk, and took the surname Guo.
units.literal: In youth he was chivalrous and bold, killed a man while drunk, was seized by the enemy family, and therefore shaved his head to become a monk and usurped the surname Guo.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：入蔡賊中，為賊帥假子，更姓名為郭禹。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says he joined the Cai rebels as an adopted son and renamed himself Guo Yu.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: entering Cai rebel bands, he became a rebel chief's adoptive son and changed his name to Guo Yu.)〉

units.zh: 亡匿久之，及貴，方復本姓。
units.en: He lived in hiding for years and only restored his true name once he had risen.
units.literal: He hid in flight a long time; when he reached eminence he then restored his original surname.

units.zh: 唐僖宗朝，為蔡州軍校，領本郡兵戍荊南，帥以其凶暴，欲害之，遂棄本軍奔於秭歸。
units.en: Under Xizong he was a Caizhou officer garrisoning Jingnan until his commander, fearing his violence, tried to kill him; he fled to Zigui with his troops.
units.literal: In Emperor Xizong's Tang he was a Cai prefecture army officer, led the prefecture's troops to garrison Jingnan; the commander because of his ferocity wished to harm him, so he abandoned his army and fled to Zigui.

units.zh: 一夕，巨蛇繞其身，幾至於殞，乃祝曰：「苟有所負，死生惟命。」
units.en: One night a giant snake coiled around him until he nearly died; he prayed, "If I am guilty, let fate decide."
units.literal: One night a huge serpent coiled around his body, almost to his death; he then prayed, saying: "If I bear some guilt, life and death are fate's alone."

units.zh: 逡巡，蛇亦解去。
units.en: In time the snake loosened and slid away.
units.literal: After a moment the serpent too unwound and left.

units.zh: 後據歸州，招集流亡，練士伍，得兵千餘人，沿流以襲荊南，遂據其地。
units.en: He took Guizhou, rallied refugees into a thousand-man force, sailed downriver against Jingnan, and seized it.
units.literal: Later he seized Guizhou, gathered fugitives, drilled soldiers, obtained more than a thousand troops, along the river struck Jingnan, and thus held that territory.

units.zh: 朝廷即以旄鉞授之。
units.en: The court soon invested him with full military command.
units.literal: The court at once granted him command pennant and axe.

units.zh: 是時荊州經巨盜之後，居民才一十七家，汭撫輯凋殘，勵精為理，通商訓農，勤於惠養，比及末年，僅及萬戶。
units.en: Jingzhou after the great devastations held only seventeen households; Rui rebuilt trade and agriculture until, by his last years, the city neared ten thousand families.
units.literal: At that time Jingzhou after great bandits had only seventeen resident households; Rui pacified the devastated ruin, strove in governance, opened commerce and trained farming, diligently in nurturing kindness—by his last years barely reaching ten thousand households.

units.zh: 汭性豪暴，事皆意斷，又好自矜伐，騁辯淩人，深為識者所鄙。
units.en: Rui was domineering, arrogant in debate, and widely scorned by men of judgment.
units.literal: Rui's nature was arrogant and violent; affairs were all decided by his own intent; he also loved self-praise, vaunted eloquence to overbear others, and was deeply despised by the knowing.

units.zh: 初，澧、朗二州，本屬荊南，乾寧中，為土豪雷滿所據。
units.en: Li and Lang, once part of Jingnan, fell to the local strongman Lei Man in Qianning.
units.literal: At first Li and Lang two prefectures originally belonged to Jingnan; in Qianning they were held by local strongman Lei Man.

units.zh: 汭奏請割隸，唐宰相徐彥若執而不行，汭由是銜之。
units.en: Rui asked the court to annex them; Chancellor Xu Yanruo refused, and Rui nursed a grudge.
units.literal: Rui memorialized requesting to detach and subordinate them; Tang chancellor Xu Yanruo held firm and did not carry it out; Rui thereby harbored resentment.

units.zh: 及彥若出鎮南海，路過江陵，汭雖加延接，而猶怏怏。
units.en: When Yanruo passed Jiangling en route to his Nanhai post, Rui received him coldly despite the courtesies.
units.literal: When Yanruo went out to command Nanhai, passing Jiangling, Rui though adding courtesies was still displeased.

units.zh: 嘗因對酒，語及其事，彥若曰：「令公位尊方面，自比桓、文。
units.en: At wine Yanruo said, "You rank yourself with Duke Huan and Duke Wen of Qi and Jin.
units.literal: Once over wine he spoke of the matter; Yanruo said: "My lord's position is honored in your quarter, comparing yourself to Huan and Wen.

units.zh: 雷滿者，偏州一草賊爾，令公盍不加兵，而反怨朝廷乎！」
units.en: Yet you resent the court over Lei Man, a mere frontier bandit—why not march against him instead?"
units.literal: Lei Man is but a petty prefecture grass bandit—why does my lord not send troops instead of resenting the court!"

units.zh: 汭赧然而屈。
units.en: Rui flushed and fell silent.
units.literal: Rui blushed and was subdued.

units.zh: 〈（案：以下有闕文。）〉
units.en: (The text below is lost.)〉
units.literal: (Note: Below there is missing text.)〉

units.zh: 累官至檢校太尉，封上穀郡王。
units.en: He rose to honorary Grand Commandant and was made Prince of Shanggu.
units.literal: In succession he reached honorary Grand General and was enfeoffed Prince of Shanggu commandery.

units.zh: 楊行密以兵圍鄂州，汭出師以援鄂，淮寇乘之，以火焚其艦，汭投江而死。
units.en: When Yang Xingmi besieged Ezhou, Rui sailed to relieve it; the Huainan fleet burned his ships and he drowned himself in the river.
units.literal: Yang Xingmi with troops besieged Ezhou; Rui marched out to relieve E; Huainan raiders seized the moment, used fire to burn his warships; Rui threw himself in the river and died.

units.zh: 天祐三年夏，太祖以汭歿於王事，上表於唐帝，請為汭立廟於荊門，優詔可之。
units.en: Tianyou 3, summer: the Founder had the Tang court approve a temple for Rui at Jingmen, honoring his death in service.
units.literal: In summer of Tianyou year 3 the Founder because Rui died in royal service memorialized the Tang emperor requesting a temple for Rui at Jingmen; gracious edict approved.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：鄭準，不知何許人，性諒直，能為文章，長於箋奏。
units.en: (The 《Supplement》 says Zheng Zhun, of unknown origin, was upright, literate, and expert at memorials.
units.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Zheng Zhun, origin unknown, nature frank and upright, able at writing, skilled at memorials and reports.

units.zh: 成汭鎮荊南，辟為推官。
units.en: When Cheng Rui held Jingnan he made Zhun his investigating officer.
units.literal: Cheng Rui garrisoned Jingnan and recruited him as investigating officer.

units.zh: 汭嘗仇殺人，懼為吏所捕，改姓郭氏。
units.en: After a feud killing he had taken the surname Guo to evade the law.
units.literal: Rui once killed in feud; fearing capture by officers, changed surname to Guo.

units.zh: 及為荊南節度使，命準為表，乞歸本姓。
units.en: As Jingnan commissioner he had Zhun draft a memorial to restore the name Cheng.
units.literal: When he became Jingnan military commissioner, ordered Zhun to draft a memorial begging restoration of original surname.

units.zh: 準援筆而成，其略云：「臣門非冠蓋，家本軍戎。
units.en: Zhun wrote at once; it began, "My house wears no court caps; my family comes from the army.
units.literal: Zhun took brush and completed it; gist said: "Your subject's house is not of noble caps and canopies; family origin is military camp.

units.zh: 親朋之內，盱睢為人報怨；
units.en: Among kin and friends, eyes glaring to settle others' scores;
units.literal: Among kin and friends, glaring and gnashing to avenge others;

units.zh: 昆弟之間，點染無處求生。
units.en: Among brothers, marked with blood and nowhere to live.
units.literal: Among brothers, stained with nowhere to seek life.

units.zh: 背故國以狐疑，望鄰封而鼠竄。
units.en: I turned from my homeland in doubt and scurried to a neighbor like a cornered rat.
units.literal: Turning back on the old state in hesitant doubt, looking to neighboring borders and fleeing like a rat.

units.zh: 名非霸越，乘舟難效於陶朱；
units.en: I was no lord of Wu or Yue—by boat I could not follow Fan Li;
units.literal: Name not Ba and Yue, boarding a boat hard to emulate Tao Zhu;

units.zh: 誌切投秦，出境遂稱於張祿。」
units.en: My heart set on Qin, I crossed the border and called myself Zhang Lu."
units.literal: Aspiration keen to throw in with Qin, crossing the border then styled as Zhang Lu."

units.zh: 又云：「成為本姓，郭乃冒稱。
units.en: It added, "Cheng is my true name; Guo was a borrowed lie.
units.literal: Also said: "Cheng is the original surname; Guo is usurped claim.

units.zh: 本避犯禁之辜，敢歸司寇；
units.en: I fled a capital crime; I dare submit again to justice;
units.literal: Originally avoiding the guilt of forbidden offense, dare return to the Minister of Crime;

units.zh: 別族受封之典，誠愧諸侯。
units.en: yet to hold a fief under a false name shames me before the lords.
units.literal: Separate-surname receiving enfeoffment rites—truly ashamed before the feudal lords.

units.zh: 伏乞聖慈，許歸本姓」云云。
units.en: I kneel and beg Your Majesty to let me bear my true name again," and so on.
units.literal: Kneeling beg sacred kindness, permit restoration of original surname," etc.

units.zh: 其表甚為朝廷所重。
units.en: The court held that memorial in high regard.
units.literal: That memorial was greatly valued by the court.

units.zh: 後因汭生辰，淮南楊行密遣使致禮幣之外，仍貺《初學記》一部。
units.en: On Rui's birthday Yang Xingmi sent gifts from Huainan—and added a copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.
units.literal: Later because of Rui's birthday Huainan Yang Xingmi sent envoys with ceremonial gifts besides, still bestowing one copy of the 《Elementary Studies》.

units.zh: 準忿然以為不可，謂汭曰：「夫《初學記》，蓋訓童之書爾，今敵國交聘，以此書為貺，得非相輕之甚耶！
units.en: Zhun was furious and told Rui, "The 《Elementary Studies》 is a schoolbook for children. An enemy state sends it as a state gift—is that not open contempt?
units.literal: Zhun angrily deemed it unacceptable, told Rui: "The 《Elementary Studies》 is merely a book for instructing children; now enemy states exchange missions—using this book as a gift, is it not extreme mutual slight!

units.zh: 宜書責讓。」
units.en: You should answer with a written rebuke."
units.literal: Should write to reprove and blame."

units.zh: 汭不納，準自歎曰：「若然，見輕敵國，足彰幕府之無人也。
units.en: Rui refused. Zhun sighed, "Accept this and we show the enemy our staff has no one with spine.
units.literal: Rui did not accept; Zhun sighed to himself: "If so, being slighted by the enemy state sufficiently shows the headquarters has no men.

units.zh: 參佐無狀，安可久！」
units.en: I cannot serve such a court any longer!"
units.literal: Staff officers unworthy—how can one long remain!"

units.zh: 遽請解職。
units.en: He resigned at once.
units.literal: Hastily requested dismissal from office.

units.zh: 汭怒其去，潛使人於途中殺之。）〉
units.en: Rui, enraged, had him murdered on the road home.)〉
units.literal: Rui angry at his departure, secretly sent men on the road to kill him.)〉

units.zh: 杜洪者，江夏伶人。
units.en: Du Hong had been an entertainer in Jiangxia.
units.literal: Du Hong was a Jiangxia entertainer.

units.zh: 鍾傳者，豫章小校。
units.en: Zhong Chuan was a low officer in Yuzhang.
units.literal: Zhong Chuan was a Yuzhang junior officer.

units.zh: 唐光啟中，秦宗權凶焰飆起，屢擾江、淮，郡將不能城守。
units.en: In Guangqi, Qin Zongquan ravaged the Jiang-Huai region until prefectural garrisons could no longer hold their walls.
units.literal: In Tang Guangqi, Qin Zongquan's vicious flame rose like a whirlwind, repeatedly harassed Jiang and Huai; prefectural defenders could not hold the walls.

units.zh: 洪、傳各為部校，因戰立威，逐其廉使，自稱留後，朝廷因而命之。
units.en: Hong and Chuan rose as unit commanders, fought their way to power, expelled their superiors, declared themselves acting governors, and won court recognition.
units.literal: Hong and Chuan each were division officers; through battle established prestige, drove out their provincial inspectors, styled themselves acting governors; court thereby appointed them.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：光啟二年，洪乘虛入鄂，自為節度使留後，僖宗即拜本軍節度使。
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says that in Guangqi 2 Hong seized Ezhou, made himself acting commissioner, and Xizong confirmed him.)
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Guangqi year 2, Hong seized an opening to enter E, styled himself acting military commissioner, Emperor Xizong at once appointed him full army military commissioner.

units.zh: 中和三年，傳逐江西觀察使高茂卿，遂有洪州，僖宗擢傳江西團練使，俄拜鎮南節度使。）〉
units.en: (In Zhonghe 3 Chuan expelled Gao Maoqing from Jiangxi, took Hongzhou, and was made training commissioner, then Zhennan military commissioner.)〉
units.literal: Zhonghe year 3, Chuan drove out Jiangxi observation commissioner Gao Maoqing, then held Hongzhou; Xizong promoted Chuan Jiangxi training commissioner, soon appointed Zhennan military commissioner.)〉

units.zh: 及為楊行密所攻，洪、傳首尾相應，皆遣求援於太祖；
units.en: When Yang Xingmi attacked them, Hong and Chuan backed each other and both appealed to the Founder;
units.literal: When attacked by Yang Xingmi, Hong and Chuan head and tail responded, all sent seeking aid from the Founder;

units.zh: 太祖遣朱友恭赴之，大破淮寇於武昌，二鎮稍寧。
units.en: The Founder sent Zhu Yougong, who routed the Huainan army at Wuchang and gave the two regions brief relief.
units.literal: The Founder sent Zhu Yougong to go; greatly defeated Huainan bandits at Wuchang; the two prefectures gradually calmed.

units.zh: 及行密乘勝急攻洪、鄂，洪復乞師於太祖；
units.en: When Xingmi pressed the attack on Hong and E, Hong again begged the Founder for troops;
units.literal: When Xingmi seized victory to press attack on Hong and E, Hong again begged troops from the Founder;

units.zh: 太祖命荊南成汭率荊、襄舟師以赴之。
units.en: The Founder ordered Cheng Rui of Jingnan to sail the Jing-Xiang fleet to his aid.
units.literal: The Founder ordered Jingnan Cheng Rui to lead Jing and Xiang river fleets to go relieve.

units.zh: 未至夏口，汭敗溺死，淮人遂陷鄂州，洪為其所擒，被害於廣陵市，時唐天復二年也。
units.en: Rui drowned in defeat before Xiakou; the Huainan army took Ezhou, seized Hong, and executed him at Guangling market in Tianfu 2.
units.literal: Before reaching Xiakou, Rui was defeated and drowned; Huainan men then took Ezhou; Hong was captured by them, killed at Guangling market—then Tang Tianfu year 2.

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·劉存傳》：存急焚鄂州城樓，梁援兵將突圍而出，諸將欲急擊之，存曰：「擊之賊必復入，復入則城愈固矣，不若聽其遁去。」
units.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says Liu Cun burned Ezhou's tower as Liang relief tried to break out. His officers wanted a hard strike; Cun said, "Hit them and they will rush back in and the wall will only tighten—let them go."
units.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Liu Cun》: Cun urgently burned Ezhou's tower; Liang relief troops were about to break out; the generals wished to strike them hard; Cun said: "Strike them and the bandits will re-enter; re-enter and the city will be firmer still—better to let them escape."

units.zh: 諸將皆曰：「善。」
units.en: The generals said, "Good."
units.literal: The generals all said: "Good."

units.zh: 是日城陷，擒杜洪父子，斬於廣陵市。）〉
units.en: That day the city fell; Du Hong and his son were taken and beheaded at Guangling market.)〉
units.literal: That day the city fell; Du Hong father and son were captured and beheaded at Guangling market.)〉

units.zh: 天祐三年夏，太祖表請為洪立廟於其鎮，優詔可之。
units.en: Tianyou 3, summer: the Founder won approval for a temple to Du Hong in his old command.
units.literal: In summer of Tianyou year 3 the Founder memorialized requesting a temple for Hong at his command; gracious edict approved.

units.zh: 太祖即位，詔贈太傅。
units.en: After the Founder took the throne, Hong was posthumously named Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When the Founder took the throne, an edict posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 先是，鍾傳卒於江西，其子繼之，
units.en: Earlier Zhong Chuan had died in Jiangxi and his son succeeded him,
units.literal: Before this, Zhong Chuan died in Jiangxi; his son succeeded him,

units.zh: 〈（《九國誌·秦裴傳》：天祐三年，洪州鍾傳卒，州人立其子匡時。
units.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that in Tianyou 3 Zhong Chuan died at Hongzhou and the people set up his son Kuangshi.)
units.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Qin Pei》: Tianyou year 3, Hongzhou Zhong Chuan died; the prefecture's people installed his son Kuangshi.

units.zh: 江州刺史延規，傳之養子，忿不得立，以其郡納款，因授裴西南面行營招討使，攻匡時。
units.en: Yan Gui, Chuan's adopted son and Jiangzhou prefect, resenting his exclusion, surrendered his prefecture; Qin Pei was sent to attack Kuangshi.
units.literal: Jiangzhou prefect Yan Gui, Chuan's adoptive son, angry at not being installed, submitted his prefecture in surrender; therefore Pei was appointed southwest campaign pacification commissioner and attacked Kuangshi.

units.zh: 城陷，擒匡時以獻。）〉
units.en: The city fell and Kuangshi was captured and sent in.)〉
units.literal: The city fell; Kuangshi was captured and presented.)〉

units.zh: 尋為楊行密所敗，其地亦入於淮夷。
units.en: Soon Yang Xingmi defeated them and Jiangxi too passed to Huainan.
units.literal: Soon defeated by Yang Xingmi; that territory too entered Huainan barbarians.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：鍾傳雖起於商販，尤好學重士，時江西上流有名第者，多因傳薦，四遠騰然，謂之曰英明。
units.en: (The 《Supplement》 says Chuan began as a trader but prized learning and patronized scholars; eminent Jiangxi families often owed their posts to him, and men far and wide called him "the enlightened."
units.literal: (The 《Supplement》: Though Zhong Chuan rose from merchant peddlers, he especially loved learning and honored scholars; at that time famous clans of upper Jiangxi mostly entered through Chuan's recommendation; from the four quarters it soared—people called him "the enlightened one."

units.zh: 諸葛浩素有詞學，嘗為泗州管驛巡官，仰傳之風，因擇其所行事赫赫可稱者十條，列於啟事以投之。
units.en: Zhuge Hao, a man of letters once posted at a Sizhou relay station, admired Chuan and sent a memorial listing ten of his finest deeds.
units.literal: Zhuge Hao always had literary learning; once was Sizhou postal-station patrol officer; admiring Chuan's reputation, he therefore selected ten items from Chuan's deeds that shone and could be praised, arrayed them in a memorial to submit.

units.zh: 十啟凡五千字，皆文理典贍，傳覽之驚歎，謂賓佐曰：「此啟事每一字可以千錢酬之。」
units.en: Ten sections, five thousand characters, all polished; Chuan read them in wonder and told his staff, "Every character in this is worth a thousand cash."
units.literal: Ten memorials in all five thousand characters, all literary reasoning elegant and ample; Chuan on reading was startled and sighed, told his staff: "This memorial—each character can be rewarded with a thousand cash."

units.zh: 遂以五千貫贈，仍辟在幕下，其激勸如此。
units.en: He gave five thousand strings, took Hao onto his staff, and rewarded talent that lavishly.
units.literal: Thereupon with five thousand strings he was gifted, still recruited to the headquarters—such was his encouragement.

units.zh: 上藍和尚，失其名，居於洪州上藍院，精究術數，大為鍾傳所禮。
units.en: A monk of Shanglan Monastery in Hongzhou, name forgotten, was a master of divination whom Chuan treated with great respect.
units.literal: The Shanglan monk, his name lost, dwelt at Hongzhou Shanglan monastery, deeply studied numerology, greatly honored by Zhong Chuan.

units.zh: 一旦疾篤，往省之，且曰：「老夫於和尚可謂無間矣，和尚或不諱，得無一言相付耶！」
units.en: When the monk fell gravely ill Chuan visited him and said, "I have held nothing back from you—won't you leave me one word before you go?"
units.literal: One day gravely ill, Chuan went to visit and said: "This old man toward the monk can be said without gap—monk, if you do not mind, can you not leave one word to entrust?"

units.zh: 上藍強起，索筆作偈以援，其末云：「但看來年二三月，柳條堪作打鍾槌。」
units.en: The monk roused himself, wrote a verse, and ended it, "Watch the second or third month next year—willow twigs will do for beating the bell."
units.literal: Shanglan forced himself up, sought brush and wrote a gatha to hand over; its end said: "Only look at the second or third month of the coming year—willow branches can serve as bell-striking mallets."

units.zh: 偈終而卒。
units.en: He died as soon as the verse was finished.
units.literal: When the gatha ended he died.

units.zh: 傳得之，不能測。
units.en: Chuan could not make sense of it.
units.literal: Chuan obtained it and could not fathom it.

units.zh: 洎明年春，淮帥引兵奄至，洪州陷，江南遂為楊氏有。
units.en: Next spring the Huainan army swept in, Hongzhou fell, and the lower Yangzi passed to the Yang house.
units.literal: By the next spring the Huainan commander led troops in sudden arrival; Hongzhou fell; south of the river then belonged to the Yang clan.

units.zh: 「打鍾」之偈，人始悟焉。）〉
units.en: Only then did men grasp the "beat the bell" prophecy.)〉
units.literal: "Bell-striking" gatha—people then understood it.)〉

units.zh: 田頵，本揚府之大校也。
units.en: Tian Yun had begun as a senior officer in the Yangzhou garrison.
units.literal: Tian Yun originally was a Yang prefecture great colonel.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》：頵字德臣，廬州合肥人。）〉
units.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 gives his style Dechen and his home as Hefei in Luzhou.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States》: Yun, style name Dechen, was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.)〉

units.zh: 朱延壽，不知何許人。
units.en: Zhu Yanshou's origins are unknown.
units.literal: Zhu Yanzhou, origin unknown.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》：延壽，廬州舒城人。）〉
units.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says Yanshou came from Shucheng in Luzhou.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States》: Yanzhou was a native of Shucheng in Luzhou.)〉

units.zh: 唐天祐初，楊行密雄據淮海，時頵為宣州節度使，延壽為壽州刺史。
units.en: Early in Tianyou, Yang Xingmi dominated the Huai-Hai region; Yun held Xuancheng and Yanshou held Shou prefecture.
units.literal: Early Tang Tianyou, Yang Xingmi heroically held Huai and Hai; then Yun was Xuancheng military commissioner, Yanzhou was Shou prefect magistrate.

units.zh: 頵以行密專恣跋扈，嘗移書諷之曰：「侯王守方，以奉天子，古之制也。
units.en: Finding Yang Xingmi arrogant, Yun wrote to admonish him: "Princes are meant to guard their lands for the Son of Heaven—that is the ancient order.
units.literal: Yun because Xingmi was willful and overbearing, once sent a letter admonishing him, saying: "Marquises and kings guard their regions to serve the Son of Heaven—this is the ancient system.

units.zh: 其或逾越者，譬如百川不朝於海，雖狂奔猛注，澶漫遐廣，終為涸土，不若恬然順流，淼茫無窮也。
units.en: Whoever overreaches is like a stream that never reaches the sea: however fierce the flood, it ends in dust. Better to flow with the tide and never run dry.
units.literal: Whoever oversteps is like a hundred streams not paying court to the sea—though wildly rushing and pouring, vast and wide, in the end they become dry earth; better to calmly follow the current, boundless and without end.

units.zh: 況東南之鎮，楊為大，塵賤刀布，阜積金玉，願公上恒賦，頵將悉儲峙，具單車從。」
units.en: You are greatest in the southeast, piled with gold and goods. Send the regular tribute through me—I will store it and deliver it myself in one cart."
units.literal: Moreover among southeast commands Yang is greatest; dust and base coin and cloth, heaped gold and jade—may my lord remit the standing tax; Yun will store it all and follow with a single cart."

units.zh: 行密怒曰：「今財賦之行，必由於汴，適足以資於敵也。」
units.en: Xingmi snapped, "Revenue now must pass through Bian—that only feeds our enemy."
units.literal: Xingmi angrily said: "Now the flow of wealth and levies must pass through Bian—just enough to enrich the enemy."

units.zh: 不從。
units.en: He refused.
units.literal: He did not comply.

units.zh: 時延壽方守壽春，
units.en: Yanshou was then holding Shouchun,
units.literal: At that time Yanzhou was just defending Shouchun,

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》：天復初，北司擁駕西幸，昭宗聞延壽有武幹，遣李儼間道齎詔授延壽蔡州節度使。）〉
units.en: (The 《Nine States Chronicle》 says that early in Tianfu, with the court driven west, Zhaozong heard of Yanshou's ability and sent Li Yan secretly to name him Cai commissioner.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Chronicle of the Nine States》: Early Tianfu, the northern offices held the emperor on a western progress; Emperor Zhaozong hearing Yanzhou had martial talent sent Li Yan by hidden route bearing an edict appointing Yanzhou Cai prefecture military commissioner.)〉

units.zh: 直頵之事，密遣人告於頵曰：「公有所欲為者，願為公執鞭。」
units.en: With Yun's plot in mind, he secretly sent word: "Whatever you intend, I will serve as your man."
units.literal: Straight at Yun's affair, secretly sent men to tell Yun: "Whatever my lord wishes to do, I wish to hold the whip for my lord."

units.zh: 頵聞之，頗會其志，乃召進士杜荀鶴具述其意，復語曰：「昌本朝，奉盟主，在斯一舉矣。」
units.en: Yun took his meaning, summoned the scholar Du Xunhe, laid out the plan, and said, "To restore the dynasty and serve our ally—everything hangs on this."
units.literal: Yun on hearing greatly grasped his intent, then summoned presented scholar Du Xunhe to fully relate his intent, again saying: "To prosper the dynasty, serve the alliance lord—it's in this one move."

units.zh: 即遣荀鶴具述密議，自間道至大梁。
units.en: He sent Xunhe by secret road to Daliang with the full plot.
units.literal: At once sent Xunhe to fully relate the secret design, by hidden route to Daliang.

units.zh: 太祖大悅，遽屯兵於宿州，以會其變。
units.en: The Founder was delighted and rushed troops to Suzhou to meet the plot.
units.literal: The Founder greatly rejoiced and swiftly stationed troops at Suzhou to await their mutiny.

units.zh: 不數月，事微泄，行密乃先以公牒征延壽，
units.en: Within months the plot leaked; Xingmi summoned Yanshou by official order,
units.literal: Within not many months the matter slightly leaked; Xingmi then first with an official dispatch summoned Yanshou,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：行密妻，延壽姊也，遣辯士召延壽。
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Xingmi's wife was Yanshou's sister and sent a persuader to call him.
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Xingmi's wife was Yanshou's elder sister; he sent an eloquent man to summon Yanshou.

units.zh: 疑不肯赴，姊遣婢報，故延壽疾走揚州。）〉
units.en: Warned by his sister's maid, Yanshou galloped to Yangzhou.)〉
units.literal: Suspecting he would not come, the sister sent a maid to report; therefore Yanshou galloped posthaste to Yangzhou.)〉

units.zh: 次悉兵攻宣城，頵戎力寡薄，棄壁走，不能越境，為行密軍所得。
units.en: Xingmi then attacked Xuancheng; Yun, outmatched, fled the walls but was caught before he could escape the prefecture.
units.literal: Next he marshaled all troops to attack Xuancheng; Yun's defending strength was thin and few—he abandoned the walls and fled, could not cross the border, and was taken by Xingmi's army.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》：行密別遣台濛、王茂章率步騎以往，頵委舟師於汪建、王壇，自出廣德迎戰，大為濛所敗，遂率殘眾遁保宛陵。
units.en: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says Xingmi sent Tai Meng and Wang Maozhang by land; Yun entrusted the fleet to Wang Jian and Wang Tan, then fought at Guangde, was routed, and fled to Wanyang with survivors.
units.literal: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》: Xingmi separately sent Tai Meng and Wang Maozhang leading foot and horse to go; Yun entrusted the fleet to Wang Jian and Wang Tan, himself going out from Guangde to meet battle, and was greatly defeated by Meng; he then led remnant masses to flee and hold Wanyang.

units.zh: 壇、建聞其敗，因盡以舟師歸款於行密。
units.en: Wang Tan and Wang Jian heard of the defeat and surrendered the whole fleet to Xingmi.
units.literal: Tan and Jian heard of his defeat and therefore entirely with the fleet submitted to Xingmi.

units.zh: 十二月，頵出外州柵疾戰，橋陷馬墜，為外軍所殺。）〉
units.en: In the twelfth month Yun fought at the outer stockade; the bridge gave way, his horse fell, and the besiegers killed him.)〉
units.literal: Twelfth month, Yun went out of Wai prefecture stockade to fight fiercely; the bridge collapsed and his horse fell—he was killed by the outer army.)〉

units.zh: 延壽飛騎赴命，邇揚州一舍，行密使人殺之。
units.en: Yanshou galloped toward Yangzhou; a stage short of the city, Xingmi's men killed him.
units.literal: Yanshou with flying horse rushed to answer the summons; nearing Yangzhou by one stage, Xingmi sent men to kill him.

units.zh: 其後，延壽部曲有逸境至者，具言其事。
units.en: Later fugitives from Yanshou's command told the full story.
units.literal: Afterward, of Yanshou's division there were those who escaped the border and came, fully narrating this affair.

units.zh: 又云：延壽之將行也，其室王氏勉延壽曰：「今若得兵柄，果成大志，是吉凶係乎時，非係於吾家也。
units.en: They said that before he left, his wife Lady Wang urged him: "If you win command and your great ambition succeeds, fortune and ruin ride on the times, not on our house.
units.literal: They also said: When Yanshou was about to depart, his wife the Wang clan urged Yanshou saying: "Now if you obtain military power and indeed achieve a great ambition, fortune and misfortune depend on the times, not on our household.

units.zh: 然願日致一介，以寧所懷。」
units.en: Yet send me one messenger each day to ease my heart."
units.literal: Yet I wish each day to send one messenger, to quiet what the heart holds."

units.zh: 一日，介不至，王氏曰：「事可知矣！」
units.en: When a day passed without word, Lady Wang said, "The matter is clear!"
units.literal: One day no messenger came; Lady Wang said: "The matter can be known!"

units.zh: 乃部分家仆，悉授兵器，遽闔中扉，而捕騎已至，不得入。
units.en: She armed the household, bolted the inner doors, and kept the arresting horsemen outside.
units.literal: She then arrayed the household servants, all gave weapons, swiftly shut the inner doors—and the arresting horsemen had already arrived, could not enter.

units.zh: 遂集家屬，阜私帑，發百燎，合州廨焚之。
units.en: She gathered her kin, piled the family treasury, lit a hundred fires, and burned the prefectural offices with them.
units.literal: Thereupon she gathered kin, heaped private treasuries, lit a hundred torches, and together with the prefectural offices burned them.

units.zh: 既而稽首上告曰：「妾誓不以皎然之軀，為仇者所辱。」
units.en: Kowtowing, she declared, "I will not let my enemies dishonor this body."
units.literal: Then she kowtowed upward and declared: "This wife vows not to let this pure body be shamed by enemies."

units.zh: 乃投火而死。
units.en: She threw herself into the flames and died.
units.literal: Thereupon she cast herself into the fire and died.

units.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：楊行密據淮南，以妻弟朱氏眾謂之朱三郎者，行密署為泗州防禦使。
units.en: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says Xingmi made his brother-in-law Zhu, called Third Master Zhu, defense commissioner of Sizhou.
units.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Yang Xingmi held Huainan; his wife's younger brother of the Zhu clan, whom the masses called Zhu the Third, Xingmi appointed defense commissioner of Sizhou.

units.zh: 泗州素屯軍，朱氏驍勇，到任恃眾自負，行密雖悔，度力未能製，但姑息之，時議以謂行密事勢去矣。
units.en: Sizhou was garrison country; Zhu was fierce and swaggered in office while Xingmi, unable to curb him, only indulged him—observers thought Xingmi had lost his grip.
units.literal: Sizhou always quartered troops; the Zhu clan was fierce and brave—on reaching office he relied on the masses and was self-important; Xingmi though regretted it, gauged his strength could not control him, only indulged him; at the time opinion held that Xingmi's situation and power were gone.

units.zh: 居無何，行密得目疾，雖愈，且詐稱失明，其出入皆以人扶策，不爾則觸牆抵柱，至於流血，姬妾仆隸以為實然，往往無禮，首尾僅三年。
units.en: Soon he suffered an eye ailment; though healed, he feigned blindness for nearly three years, needing guides and colliding with walls until servants and concubines took it for truth and grew insolent.
units.literal: After not long, Xingmi contracted eye disease; though cured, he yet falsely claimed blindness; going in and out he was always supported by men, otherwise he would strike walls and pillars, even to bleeding; concubines and servants thought it real and often were without propriety—for head and tail nearly three years.

units.zh: 朱氏聞之，信而少懈馳，行密度其計必中，謂妻曰：「吾不幸臨老兩目如此，男女輩幼，苟不諱，則國家為他人所有。
units.en: Zhu believed the blindness and relaxed his guard; Xingmi, sure his ruse had worked, told his wife: "I am old and blind, the children young—if we do not act, our realm will pass to another.
units.literal: The Zhu clan heard it, believed it, and slightly slackened vigilance; Xingmi gauged his plan would surely hit, and told his wife: "I am unlucky to face old age with both eyes thus; the boys and girls are young—if we do not take care, then the state will belong to others.

units.zh: 今晝夜思忖，不如召泗州三舅來，使管勾軍府事，則吾雖死無恨。」
units.en: Better summon your third brother from Sizhou to run headquarters—then I can die content."
units.literal: Now day and night I ponder—better to summon the third maternal uncle from Sizhou to manage military headquarters affairs; then though I die I have no regret."

units.zh: 妻以為然，遽發使述其意而召之。
units.en: She agreed and sent envoys to summon him.
units.literal: The wife thought it right and swiftly sent envoys stating the intent and summoned him.

units.zh: 朱氏大喜，倍道而至。
units.en: Zhu was overjoyed and came at forced march.
units.literal: The Zhu clan greatly rejoiced and came by double stages.

units.zh: 及入謁，行密恐其覺，坐於中堂，以家人禮見。
units.en: Fearing discovery, Xingmi received him in the central hall with family rites.
units.literal: When he entered to pay respects, Xingmi feared he would detect it; he sat in the central hall and received him with family ceremony.

units.zh: 朱氏頗有德色，方設拜，行密奮袖中鐵槌以擊之，正中其首，然猶宛轉號叫，久而方斃。
units.en: As Zhu bowed, Xingmi struck him from his sleeve with an iron mallet; Zhu twisted and screamed a long while before he died.
units.literal: The Zhu clan had quite a virtuous countenance; just as he set to bow, Xingmi whipped out an iron mallet from his sleeve to strike him—square on the head; yet he still twisted and cried out, long before finally dead.

units.zh: 行密內外不測，即時升堂廳，召將吏等謂之曰：「吾所以稱兩目失明者，蓋為朱三。
units.en: The court was stunned; Xingmi mounted the hall and told his officers: "I only pretended blindness for Zhu the Third.
units.literal: Inside and outside Xingmi's court could not fathom it; he at once ascended the hall chamber and summoned generals and clerks, telling them: "The reason I claimed both eyes blind was all for Zhu the Third.

units.zh: 此賊今擊殺，兩目無事矣，諸公知之否！」
units.en: That traitor is dead and my eyes are sound—do you understand?"
units.literal: This villain is now struck dead; both eyes are unharmed—do you gentlemen know it or not!"

units.zh: 於是軍府大駭，其仆妾嘗所無禮者皆自殺。
units.en: The headquarters panicked; servants and concubines who had been insolent killed themselves.
units.literal: Thereupon the military headquarters was greatly alarmed; the servants and concubines who had been without propriety all killed themselves.

units.zh: 初，行密之在民間也，嘗為合肥縣手力，有過，縣令將鞭之，行密懼且拜。
units.en: Once, as a corvée laborer in Hefei county, he faced a magistrate's whip and bowed in terror.
units.literal: At first, when Xingmi was among the people, he had been a Hefei county corvée laborer; he had an offense and the county magistrate was about to whip him—Xingmi feared and bowed.

units.zh: 會有客自外入，見行密每拜，則廳之前簷皆叩地，而令不之覺。
units.en: A visitor saw each bow shake the eaves to the ground while the magistrate noticed nothing.
units.literal: A guest came in from outside and saw each time Xingmi bowed, then the hall's front eaves all struck the ground, while the magistrate did not notice.

units.zh: 客知其非常，乃遽升廳揖令於他處，告以所見，令驚，遂恕之，且勸事郡以自奮。
units.en: The guest knew him extraordinary, warned the magistrate, won a pardon, and urged him to serve the prefecture.
units.literal: The guest knew he was extraordinary and swiftly ascended the hall to bow to the magistrate elsewhere, reporting what he had seen; the magistrate was alarmed, then pardoned him and also urged him to serve the commandery to exert himself.

units.zh: 行密度本郡不足依，乃投高駢。
units.en: Finding Hefei too small, he entered Gao Pian's service.
units.literal: Xingmi gauged his native commandery insufficient to rely on and thereupon submitted to Gao Pian.

units.zh: 駢死，秦彥、孫儒等作亂，行密連誅之，遂有淮南之地。）〉
units.en: After Pian's death he destroyed Qin Yan and Sun Ru and seized Huainan.)〉
units.literal: Pian died; Qin Yan, Sun Ru, and others made disorder—Xingmi in succession executed them and thereupon had the Huainan lands.)〉

units.zh: 趙匡凝，
units.en: Next was Zhao Kuangning,
units.literal: Zhao Kuangning,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：匡凝字光儀。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 gives his style as Guangyi.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》: Kuangning's style name was Guangyi.)〉

units.zh: 蔡州人也。
units.en: was a native of Cai prefecture.
units.literal: was a man of Cai prefecture.

units.zh: 父德諲，初事秦宗權為列校，當宗權強暴時，表為襄州留後。
units.en: His father Dexin served Qin Zongquan as a column commander and was made acting commissioner of Xiang when Zongquan grew violent.
units.literal: Father Dexin at first served Qin Zongquan as a column commander; when Zongquan was violent and fierce, he memorialized him as Xiangzhou acting commissioner.

units.zh: 唐光啟四年夏六月，德諲審宗權必敗，乃舉漢南之地以歸唐朝，仍遣使投分於太祖，兼誓戮力，同討宗權。
units.en: In summer, month 6 of Guangqi 4, Dexin saw Zongquan would fall, surrendered Hannan to Tang, sent envoys to the Founder, and swore to destroy Zongquan together.
units.literal: Tang Guangqi year 4 summer sixth month, Dexin judged Zongquan would surely be defeated and thereupon raised the Hannan lands to return to Tang, still sending envoys to declare separation to the Founder and jointly swearing united strength to attack Zongquan together.

units.zh: 時太祖為蔡州四面行營都統使，乃表德諲為副，仍領襄州節度使。
units.en: The Founder, then overall commander against Cai, made Dexin his deputy and confirmed him as Xiang commissioner.
units.literal: At that time the Founder was Caizhou four-sides campaign overall commander; he memorialized Dexin as deputy and still had him lead Xiangzhou military commissioner.

units.zh: 蔡州平，以功累加官爵，封淮安王。
units.en: After Cai fell he rose in rank and was enfeoffed Prince of Huai'an.
units.literal: When Cai prefecture was pacified, by merit offices and titles were repeatedly added; he was enfeoffed Prince of Huai'an.

units.zh: 匡凝以父功為唐州刺史兼七州馬步軍都校。
units.en: Kuangning became Tang prefect inspector and overall commander of seven prefectures' horse and foot through his father's merit.
units.literal: Kuangning by his father's merit was Tang prefecture inspector and concurrent seven-prefecture horse-and-foot army overall commander.

units.zh: 及德諲卒，匡凝自為襄州留後，朝廷即以旄鉞授之。
units.en: When Dexin died Kuangning made himself acting commissioner and received the court commission.
units.literal: When Dexin died, Kuangning made himself Xiangzhou acting commissioner; the court thereupon bestowed the command baton and axe.

units.zh: 作鎮數年，甚有威惠，累官至檢校太尉、兼中書令。
units.en: He ruled Xiang for years with authority and kindness and rose to Honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: As commissioner for several years he had great authority and kindness; offices repeatedly reached Honorary Grand Marshal and concurrent Central Secretariat Director.

units.zh: 匡凝氣貌甚偉，好自修飾，每整衣冠，必使人持巨鑒前後照之。
units.en: Tall and vain, he had great mirrors held before and behind him whenever he dressed.
units.literal: Kuangning's bearing was very grand; he loved self-adornment—each time he arranged cap and robes he must have men hold great mirrors before and behind to shine on him.

units.zh: 對客之際，烏巾上微覺有塵，即令侍妓持紅拂以去之。
units.en: If he sensed dust on his black cap before guests, maids brushed it away with red dusters.
units.literal: When facing guests, on the black cap he slightly sensed dust and at once ordered serving girls to hold red dusters to remove it.

units.zh: 人有誤犯其家諱者，往往遭其木檟楚，其方嚴也如是。
units.en: Anyone who breached his name taboo risked a beating with a wooden club.
units.literal: Those who by mistake violated his family taboo often suffered his wooden cudgel beating—his severity was thus.

units.zh: 光化初，匡凝以太祖有清口之敗，密附於淮夷，太祖遣氏叔琮率師伐之。
units.en: Early in Guanghua, after the Founder's defeat at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly sided with the Huai rebels and the Founder sent Shi Shucong against him.
units.literal: At the start of Guanghua, because the Founder had been defeated at Qingkou, Kuangning secretly attached himself to the Huai forces; the Founder sent Shi Shucong with troops to attack him.

units.zh: 未幾，其泌州刺史趙璠越墉來降，隨州刺史趙匡璘臨陣就擒。
units.en: Soon his Bi inspector Zhao Fan climbed the wall to surrender and Suizhou inspector Zhao Kuanglin was taken in battle.
units.literal: Before long, his Bi prefecture inspector Zhao Fan scaled the wall to come surrender; Suizhou inspector Zhao Kuanglin at the battle line was captured on the spot.

units.zh: 俄而康懷英攻下鄧州，匡凝懼，遣使乞盟，太祖許之，自是附庸於太祖。
units.en: Kang Huaiying took Deng; Kuangning sued for peace, the Founder agreed, and he became a vassal.
units.literal: Soon Kang Huaiying attacked and took Deng prefecture; Kuangning feared and sent envoys to beg alliance—the Founder permitted it; from then he was a vassal of the Founder.

units.zh: 及成汭敗於鄂州，匡凝表其弟匡明為荊南留後。
units.en: After Cheng Rui fell at Ezhou, Kuangning had his brother Kuangming made acting Jingnan commissioner.
units.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated at E prefecture, Kuangning memorialized his younger brother Kuangming as Jingnan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 是時唐室微弱，諸道常賦多不上供，惟匡凝昆仲雖強據江山，然盡忠帝室，貢賦不絕。
units.en: While Tang weakened and most circuits withheld tribute, the Zhao brothers still sent loyal levies from their strongholds.
units.literal: At that time the Tang house was weak; many circuits' regular levies often did not go up in tribute—only Kuangning and his brothers, though strongly holding rivers and mountains, yet were wholly loyal to the imperial house and tribute and levies did not cease.

units.zh: 太祖將期受禪，以匡凝兄弟並據藩鎮，乃遣使先諭旨焉。
units.en: As the Founder prepared to take the throne, he sent envoys ahead to the Zhao brothers holding the frontier commands.
units.literal: The Founder was about to fix the date to receive the abdication mandate; because Kuangning and his brothers both held frontier commissions, he sent envoys first to announce the intent.

units.zh: 匡凝對使者流涕，答以受國恩深，豈敢隨時妄有他誌。
units.en: Kuangning wept before the envoy and said the state's grace was too deep for him to change sides with the times.
units.literal: Kuangning to the envoy wept and replied that the state's grace was deep—how dare he follow the times and rashly have another intent.

units.zh: 使者復命，太祖大怒。
units.en: The envoy returned; the Founder flew into a rage.
units.literal: The envoy returned to report; the Founder was greatly enraged.

units.zh: 天祐二年秋七月，遣楊師厚率師討之。
units.en: In autumn, month 7 of Tianyou 2, he sent Yang Shihou to attack him.
units.literal: Tianyou year 2 autumn seventh month, he sent Yang Shihou to lead troops to attack him.

units.zh: 八月，太祖親領大軍南征，仍請削匡凝在身官爵。
units.en: Month 8 the Founder marched south in person and had Kuangning stripped of rank.
units.literal: Eighth month, the Founder personally led a great army south on campaign and still requested stripping Kuangning of his personal offices and titles.

units.zh: 及師厚濟江，匡凝以兵數萬逆戰，大為師厚所敗，匡凝乃燔其舟，單舸急棹，沿漢而遁於金陵。
units.en: Shihou crossed the river; Kuangning met him with tens of thousands, was routed, burned his fleet, and fled alone up the Han to Jinling.
units.literal: When Shihou crossed the river, Kuangning with tens of thousands of troops met him in battle and was greatly defeated by Shihou; Kuangning then burned his boats, in a single skiff urgently rowed, and along the Han fled to Jinling.

units.zh: 後卒於淮南。
units.en: He later died in Huainan.
units.literal: Later he died in Huainan.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》云：師厚由陰穀伐木為梁，匡凝以兵二萬瀕江戰，大敗，乃燔州，單舸夜奔揚州。
units.en: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says Shihou bridged Yin Valley, Kuangning lost twenty thousand along the river, burned the prefecture, and fled by night to Yangzhou.
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Shihou by Yin Valley felled timber for beams; Kuangning with twenty thousand troops fought along the river, was greatly defeated, then burned the prefecture and in a single skiff fled by night to Yangzhou.

units.zh: 行密見之，曰：「君在鎮，輕車重馬輸於賊，今敗，乃歸我邪！」
units.en: Xingmi greeted him: "You fed the enemy from your post—now you come to me defeated?"
units.literal: Xingmi saw him and said: "Lord, in your commission you sent light carts and heavy horses as tribute to the enemy—now defeated, you return to me!

units.zh: 匡明亦謀奔淮南，子承規諫曰：「昔諸葛兄弟分仕二國，若適揚州，是自取疑也。」
units.en: Kuangming meant to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui warned, "Like the Zhuge brothers serving rival states, going to Yangzhou would invite suspicion."
units.literal: Kuangming also planned to flee to Huainan; his son Chenggui remonstrated: "In old times the Zhuge brothers each served a different state—if you go to Yangzhou, it is yourself inviting suspicion."

units.zh: 匡明謂然，乃趨成都。
units.en: Kuangming agreed and fled to Chengdu instead.
units.literal: Kuangming thought it so and thereupon hastened to Chengdu.

units.zh: 《歐陽史》云：行密厚遇匡凝，其後行密死，楊渥稍不禮之。
units.en: Ouyang's 《History》 says Xingmi treated Kuangning well, but after Xingmi's death Yang Wo grew rude to him.
units.literal: The 《History of Ouyang》 says: Xingmi treated Kuangning generously; afterward Xingmi died and Yang Wo gradually was without courtesy to him.

units.zh: 渥方宴食青梅，匡凝顧渥曰：「勿多食，發小兒熱。」
units.en: At a feast Wo ate green plums; Kuangning warned, "Do not eat too many—they bring fever in children."
units.literal: Wo was just feasting and eating green plums; Kuangning looked at Wo and said: "Do not eat much—it brings children's fever."

units.zh: 諸將以為慢，渥遣匡凝海陵，後為徐溫所殺。）〉
units.en: Officers took it as insult; Wo exiled him to Hailing, where Xu Wen later killed him.)〉
units.literal: The generals thought it disrespect; Wo sent Kuangning to Hailing and later Xu Wen killed him.)〉

units.zh: 初，匡凝好聚書，及敗，楊師厚獲數千卷於第，悉以來獻。
units.en: Kuangning had loved books; after his defeat Shihou seized thousands of scrolls from his house and presented them to the Founder.
units.literal: At first Kuangning loved gathering books; when defeated, Yang Shihou obtained several thousand scrolls at his residence and entirely brought them as tribute.

units.zh: 匡凝弟匡明，字讚堯，幼以父貴，一子出身，為江陵府文學。
units.en: His brother Kuangming, styled Zanyao, entered office young as a literary officer at Jiangling through their father's rank.
units.literal: Kuangning's younger brother Kuangming, style name Zanyao, in youth by his father's eminence entered office as a single son—he was Jiangling prefecture literary officer.

units.zh: 及壯，以軍功曆繡、峽二州刺史。
units.en: Grown, he won military merit as inspector of Xiuxi and Xia.
units.literal: When grown, by military merit he passed through Xiuxi and Xia prefecture inspector posts.

units.zh: 成汭之敗，其兄匡凝表為荊南留後。
units.en: After Cheng Rui's defeat his brother made him acting Jingnan commissioner.
units.literal: When Cheng Rui was defeated, his elder brother Kuangning memorialized him as Jingnan acting commissioner.

units.zh: 未至鎮，而朗、陵之兵先據其城矣。
units.en: Before he took office, Lang and Ling forces had already seized the city.
units.literal: Before he reached the commission, Lang and Ling troops had already seized the city.

units.zh: 匡明領兵逐之，遂鎮於渚宮。
units.en: Kuangming drove them off and held court at Zhugong.
units.literal: Kuangming led troops to drive them off and then held commission at Zhugong.

units.zh: 天祐二年秋，太祖既平襄州，遣楊師厚乘勝以趨荊門。
units.en: Autumn, Tianyou 2, after Xiang fell the Founder sent Shihou on toward Jingmen.
units.literal: Tianyou year 2 autumn, the Founder having pacified Xiangzhou sent Yang Shihou to ride the victory toward Jingmen.

units.zh: 匡明懼，乃舉族上峽奔蜀，王建待以賓禮。
units.en: Kuangming fled upriver to Shu with his clan; Wang Jian received him as an honored guest.
units.literal: Kuangming feared and thereupon led his clan up the gorge to flee to Shu; Wang Jian received him with guest ceremony.

units.zh: 及建稱帝，用為大理卿、工部尚書。
units.en: When Wang Jian became emperor he made him Grand Court director and Minister of Works.
units.literal: When Jian declared himself emperor, he used him as Grand Court of Review director and Works Ministry minister.

units.zh: 久之，卒於蜀。
units.en: He died in Shu many years later.
units.literal: After long time he died in Shu.

units.zh: 張佶，不知何郡人也。
units.en: Zhang Ji—his native commandery is unknown.
units.literal: Zhang Ji, not knowing what commandery man.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》，佶，京兆長安人。
units.en: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says Ji was from Chang'an in Jingzhao.
units.literal: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》, Ji was a Chang'an man of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 乾寧初，以明經中第，累遷宣州從事，復為秦宗權行軍司馬。
units.en: In early Qianning he passed the classics exam, served at Xuancheng, and became Qin Zongquan's campaign marshal.
units.literal: At the start of Qianning he passed the classics examination with honors, repeatedly rose to Xuancheng staff officer, again became Qin Zongquan campaign marshal.

units.zh: 後與劉建峰據湖南，推建峰為帥。）〉
units.en: He later seized Hunan with Liu Jianfeng and made Jianfeng commander.)〉
units.literal: Later with Liu Jianfeng he seized Hunan and pushed Jianfeng as commander.)〉

units.zh: 唐乾寧初，劉建峰據湖南，獨邵州不賓，命都將馬殷討之，期歲未克，而建峰為部下所殺，軍亂，鄰寇且至。
units.en: Early in Qianning Liu Jianfeng held Hunan while Shaozhou held out; Ma Yin besieged it a year without success, then Jianfeng was murdered, the army mutinied, and enemies closed in.
units.literal: At the start of Tang Qianning, Liu Jianfeng held Hunan; only Shaozhou would not submit; he ordered capital commander Ma Yin to attack it—a year passed without taking it, and Jianfeng was killed by subordinates, the army in disorder, neighboring enemies about to arrive.

units.zh: 是時，佶為行軍司馬，屬潭人謀帥，曰：「張行軍即所奉也。」
units.en: Ji was campaign marshal; the Tan garrison chose him, saying, "We want Commander Zhang."
units.literal: At that time Ji was campaign marshal; Tan men plotted a commander, saying: "Campaign Commander Zhang is whom we uphold."

units.zh: 佶不得已而視事，旬日之間，威聲大振，寇亦解去。
units.en: Ji took command unwillingly; within ten days his authority restored order and the enemies withdrew.
units.literal: Ji had no way but to take office; within ten days authority and renown greatly shook, and the enemies also withdrew.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》，建峰將吏推佶為帥，佶將入府，常所乘馬忽爾踶齧不止，正中佶髀。
units.en: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》 says as Ji entered headquarters his usual mount kicked and bit him square in the thigh.
units.literal: (The 《Nine Kingdoms Annals》, Jianfeng's generals and clerks pushed Ji as commander; Ji was about to enter headquarters when the horse he always rode suddenly kicked and bit without stop, squarely striking Ji's thigh.

units.zh: 佶謂將吏曰：「吾非汝主，當迎馬公為之。」）〉
units.en: Ji told the officers, "I am not your lord—bring Lord Ma." )〉
units.literal: Ji told the generals and clerks: "I am not your lord—you should welcome Lord Ma for it." )〉

units.zh: 乃謂將吏曰：「佶才能不如馬公，況朝廷重藩，非其人不可。」
units.en: He told them, "I am no match for Ma Yin, and the court needs the right man for a frontier post."
units.literal: He then told the generals and clerks: "Ji's talent is not equal to Lord Ma's; moreover the court weighs frontier commissions—not a non-person can hold it."

units.zh: 因以牘召，殷亦不疑，稟命而至。
units.en: He summoned Yin by document; Yin came without suspicion.
units.literal: Thereupon with a document he summoned him; Yin also did not doubt and received orders and came.

units.zh: 佶受拜謁，禮畢，命升階讓殷為帥。
units.en: Ji received his bow, then stepped aside and installed Yin as commander.
units.literal: Ji received his bow and courtesy; when ceremony finished he ordered ascending the steps and yielded Yin as commander.

units.zh: 佶即趨下率眾抃賀。
units.en: Ji hurried below and led the troops in acclaim.
units.literal: Ji at once hurried down and led the masses in clapping congratulations.

units.zh: 乃自請率師代殷攻邵州，下之。
units.en: He then led troops in Yin's place, took Shaozhou, and delivered it.
units.literal: He then himself requested to lead troops in Yin's stead to attack Shaozhou and took it.

units.zh: 復為行軍司馬，垂二十年。
units.en: He served again as campaign marshal for nearly twenty years.
units.literal: Again he was campaign marshal—for nearly twenty years.

units.zh: 殷果立勳，甚德佶。
units.en: Yin prospered and held Ji in deep esteem.
units.literal: Yin indeed established merit and deeply esteemed Ji.

units.zh: 開平初，殷表佶為朗州永順軍節度使，累加檢校太傅、同平章事。
units.en: Early in Kaiping Yin made him military commissioner of Langzhou's Yongshun army and Honorary Grand Tutor and Secretariat Fellow.
units.literal: At the start of Kaiping, Yin memorialized Ji as Langzhou Yongshun army military commissioner; offices repeatedly added Honorary Grand Tutor and Fellow of the Secretariat Chancellery.

units.zh: 乾化元年夏四月，卒於位。
units.en: Qianhua 1, summer month 4, he died in office.
units.literal: In Qianhua year 1, summer, fourth month, he died in office.

units.zh: 〈（《九國志》：乾化初，移鎮桂林，卒於治所。）〉
units.en: (The 《Nine States》 says he moved to Guilin early in Qianhua and died at his headquarters.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Histories of the Nine States》 says: At the beginning of Qianhua he was transferred to govern Guilin and died at his seat of government.)〉

units.zh: 詔贈侍中。
units.en: The court posthumously made him Chamberlain Attendant.
units.literal: An edict posthumously granted Chamberlain Attendant.

units.zh: 雷滿，
units.en: Lei Man,
units.literal: Lei Man,

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：滿字秉仁。）〉
units.en: (The 《New Tang History》 gives his style as Bingren.)〉
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Man's style name was Bingren.)〉

units.zh: 武陵洞蠻也。
units.en: came from the Wuling cave tribes.
units.literal: was a cave-barbarian of Wuling.

units.zh: 始為朗州小校，唐廣明初，王仙芝焚劫江陵。
units.en: He began as a Langzhou corporal; when Wang Xianzhi sacked Jiangling in early Guangming,
units.literal: At first he was a petty officer of Lang prefecture; at the beginning of Tang Guangming, Wang Xianzhi burned and plundered Jiangling.

units.zh: 是時，朝廷以高駢為節度使，駢擢滿為裨將，以領蠻軍。
units.en: the court sent Gao Pian as commissioner, and Pian made Man a deputy to lead tribal levies.
units.literal: At that time the court appointed Gao Pian military commissioner; Pian promoted Man to deputy general to lead barbarian troops.

units.zh: 駢移鎮淮南，復隸部曲，以悍獷趫健知名。
units.en: When Pian moved south, Man stayed in his retinue and won fame for ferocious speed.
units.literal: When Pian shifted his garrison to Huainan, Man again belonged to his command; for fierce and unruly speed and strength he was famed.

units.zh: 中和初，擅率部兵自廣陵逃歸於朗，沿江恣殘暴，始為荊人大患矣。
units.en: Early Zhonghe he deserted Guangling for Langzhou and raided the Yangzi—Jing's nightmare had begun.
units.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe he on his own led his troops to flee from Guangling back to Lang, along the river wantonly cruel and violent, beginning to be a great affliction to the people of Jing.

units.zh: 率一歲中三四移，兵入其郛，焚蕩驅掠而去。
units.en: Three or four times a year his armies burned the suburbs and drove off the plunder.
units.literal: Leading troops three or four times in a year he moved; when troops entered their outer walls they burned, swept, drove, and plundered and left.

units.zh: 唐朝姑務息兵，即以澧朗節度使授之。
units.en: Tang bought peace and gave him the Li-Lang commission.
units.literal: The Tang court for the moment pursued resting arms and thereupon granted him the Li and Lang military commissioner.

units.zh: 累官至檢校太傅、同平章事。
units.en: He rose to honorary Grand Preceptor and Vice Grand Councilor.
units.literal: By accumulation of office he reached honorary Grand Preceptor and Associate Director of the Department of State Affairs.

units.zh: 滿貪穢慘毒，蓋非人類。
units.en: Man's greed and cruelty were scarcely human.
units.literal: Man was greedy, foul, and cruelly poisonous—surely no human kind.

units.zh: 又嘗於府署浚一深潭，構大亭於其上，每鄰道使車經由，必召宴於中，且言：「此水府也，中有蛟龍，奇怪萬態，惟餘能遊焉。」
units.en: He dug a deep pool at headquarters and built a pavilion over it; when envoys passed through he always feasted them there and boasted, "This is my water palace, full of dragons in ten thousand shapes—only I can swim it."
units.literal: Again he once at the prefectural office dug a deep pool, built a great pavilion upon it; whenever neighboring circuit envoys' carriages passed through, he inevitably summoned them to feast within, and moreover said: "This is the water palace; within are flood-dragons, myriad strange forms—only I can roam it."

units.zh: 或酒酣對客，即取筵中寶器亂擲於潭中，因自褫其衣，裸露其文身，遽躍入水底，遍取所擲寶器，戲弄於水面，久之方出，復整衣就坐，其詭誕如此。
units.en: When drunk he would hurl gold and jade from the table into the pool, strip to show his tattoos, dive after them, juggle them on the surface, then dress and sit down again—as grotesque as that.
units.literal: Sometimes when wine was deep facing guests, he at once took precious vessels from the feast and wildly threw them into the pool, then himself stripped his clothes, bared his tattooed body, abruptly leaped into the water bottom, everywhere took up the thrown precious vessels, sported with them on the water surface, long after only emerged, again straightened clothes and took seat—his freakish absurdity was thus.

units.zh: 及死，子彥恭繼之。
units.en: At his death his son Yiangong took over.
units.literal: When he died, his son Yiangong succeeded him.

units.zh: 〈（《新唐書》：滿以天復元年卒，子彥威自立，弟彥恭結忠義節度使趙匡凝以逐彥威。）〉
units.en: (The New Tang History says: Man died in Tianfu 1; his son Yanwei established himself; Yanwei's younger brother Yiangong joined Loyalty and Righteousness military commissioner Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei.)
units.literal: (The 《New Book of Tang》 says: Man died in Tianfu year 1; son Yanwei established himself; younger brother Yiangong joined Loyalty and Righteousness military commissioner Zhao Kuangning to drive out Yanwei.)〉

units.zh: 蠻蜒狡獪，深有父風，燼墟落，榜舟楫，上下於南郡、武昌之間，殆無人矣。
units.en: Savage and sly like his father, he burned villages and raided by boat between Nanjun and Wuchang until hardly anyone remained.
units.literal: A crafty southern barbarian, deeply having his father's manner: burning ruins and villages, plying boats and oars, up and down between Nanjun and Wuchang—nearly no people remained.

units.zh: 又與淮、蜀結連，阻絕王命。
units.en: He allied with Huai and Shu and blocked the court's orders.
units.literal: Again he linked with Huai and Shu, obstructing and cutting off the royal commands.

units.zh: 太祖詔湖南節度使馬殷、荊南節度使高季昌練精兵五千，遣將倪可福統之，下澧州，與潭兵合。
units.en: The Founder ordered Ma Yin and Gao Jichang to send five thousand elite troops under Ni Kefu to take Li and join the Tan army.
units.literal: The Founder issued an edict ordering Hunan military commissioner Ma Yin and Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jichang to drill five thousand elite troops, send general Ni Kefu to command them, descend on Li prefecture, and unite with the Tan troops.

units.zh: 先是，滿塹沅江，以周其壘，門臨長橋，勢不可入。
units.en: Man had moated the Yuan around his walls; the gate on the long bridge was impregnable.
units.literal: Earlier Man had moated the Yuan River to surround his ramparts; the gate faced a long bridge—momentum could not enter.

units.zh: 殷極其兵力，攻圍周歲，彥恭食盡兵敗，間使求救於淮夷。
units.en: Yin besieged a full year; starving and beaten, Yiangong sent to the Huai for aid.
units.literal: Yin exhausted his military strength; attack and siege a full year; Yiangong food exhausted, troops defeated, through envoys begged rescue from the Huai barbarians.

units.zh: 及淮軍來援，高季昌逆戰於治津馬頭岸，大破之，俄而攻陷朗州，彥恭單棹遁去。
units.en: When Huai reinforcements came, Gao Jichang routed them at Matou Bank, then took Langzhou as Yiangong fled alone in a skiff.
units.literal: When Huai troops came to rescue, Gao Jichang met them in battle at Zhijin Matou Bank and greatly defeated them; soon he attacked and took Lang prefecture; Yiangong in a single punt fled away.

units.zh: 馬殷擒其弟彥雄及逆黨七人，械送至闕，皆斬於汴橋下，時開平二年十一月也。
units.en: Ma Yin seized Yanxiong and seven rebels, sent them to Bian—all were executed at Bian Bridge in Kaiping 2, month 11.
units.literal: Ma Yin captured his younger brother Yanxiong and seven rebel partisans, sent them in shackles to the capital—all were beheaded below Bian Bridge; it was Kaiping year 2, eleventh month.

units.zh: 史臣曰：成汭、鍾、杜、田、朱之流，皆因否運，雄據大藩，雖無濟代之勞，且有勤王之節，功雖不就，誌亦可嘉，若較其誠明，則田頵、延壽斯為優矣。
units.en: The historian writes: Cheng Rui, Zhong, Du, Tian, Zhu and the like seized great domains in dark times; they lacked power to save the realm yet showed loyalty to the throne; merit failed but intent deserves praise—of them Tian Yun and Yanshou showed the truest hearts.
units.literal: The historian says: Cheng Rui, Zhong, Du, Tian, Zhu, and their kind all because of adverse fortune boldly held great circuits; although they had no merit of saving the age, yet they had the integrity of assisting the king; achievement although not accomplished, intention also may be praised—if comparing their sincerity and clarity, then Tian Yun and Yanshou are superior.

units.zh: 匡凝一門昆仲，千里江山，失守藩垣，不克負荷，斯乃劉景升之子之徒歟！
units.en: The Kuangning brothers held a thousand li yet lost their domain and could not sustain it—were they not Liu Biao's sons reborn?
units.literal: Kuangning one family's brothers, a thousand li of rivers and mountains, lost guard of the frontier walls, could not bear the burden—is this not the sort of Liu Jingsheng's sons!

units.zh: 張佶有讓帥之賢，雷滿辱俾侯之寄，優劣可知矣。
units.en: Zhang Ji showed the grace to yield command; Lei Man shamed the trust of a commissioner—the contrast tells all.
units.literal: Zhang Ji had the virtue of yielding command; Lei Man disgraced the entrustment of vice-lord—superior and inferior can be known.

units.zh: 光化元年三月，太祖令往光州說刺史劉存背淮賊以向國，又從李彥威復黃州及武昌縣，獲刺史瞿章。
units.en: In the third month of Guanghua 1 the Founder sent him to Guangzhou to urge Liu Cun to abandon the Huai rebels for the throne; he then joined Li Yanwei in retaking Huangzhou and Wuchang county and took Prefect Qu Zhang captive.
units.literal: Guanghua 1 third month, the Founder sent him to Guang prefecture to persuade Prefect Liu Cun to turn from Huai bandits toward the state; he also followed Li Yanwei to recover Huang prefecture and Wuchang county and captured Prefect Qu Zhang.

units.zh: 會淮賊急攻光州，存與嗣勳率兵大戰，敗而走之。
units.en: When Huai rebels stormed Guangzhou, Liu Cun and Sixun gave battle and routed them.
units.literal: When Huai bandits pressed Guang prefecture in force, Cun and Sixun led troops in great battle and defeated and drove them off.

units.zh: 俄復使光州，持幣馬以賜劉存。
units.en: He was soon dispatched to Guangzhou again with gifts of silk and horses for Liu Cun.
units.literal: Soon he was again sent to Guang prefecture, bearing silks and horses to bestow on Liu Cun.

units.zh: 二年八月，太祖討趙匡凝於襄陽，命師厚統前軍以進，趙匡凝嚴兵以備。
units.en: In the eighth month of year 2 the Founder attacked Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang and put Shihou at the head of the advance; Kuangning drew up in full strength.
units.literal: Year 2, eighth month, the Founder campaigned against Zhao Kuangning at Xiangyang and ordered Shihou to lead the vanguard forward; Zhao Kuangning arrayed his troops in readiness.

units.zh: 一戰，趙匡凝敗散，攜妻子沿漢遁去。
units.en: One engagement broke Kuangning's army; he fled down the Han with his family.
units.literal: In one battle Zhao Kuangning was routed and scattered; he took wife and children and fled along the Han.

units.zh: 〈（《舊唐書》：天祐三年六月甲申，敕：「襄州近因趙匡凝作帥，請別立忠義軍額，既非往製，固是縱權，忠義軍額宜停廢，依舊為山南東道節度使。」）〉
units.en: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 records that on jiashen in the sixth month of Tianyou 3 an edict declared: "Because Zhao Kuangning lately became commander at Xiangzhou and sought a separate Loyal and Righteous Army commission—neither the former institution nor anything but usurped authority—the Loyal and Righteous Army title should be abolished and Xiang restored to the Shannan East Circuit military commissioner.")
units.literal: (The 《Old Book of Tang》 says: Tianyou year 3, sixth month, day jiashen, an edict: "Xiangzhou lately, because Zhao Kuangning became commander, asked to establish separately the title of the Loyal and Righteous Army; this is neither the former system nor anything but usurped authority—the Loyal and Righteous Army title should be abolished and the former Shannan East Circuit military commissioner restored.")

units.zh: 是時梁有敬翔，燕有馬鬱，華州有李巨川，荊南有鄭準，
units.en: Liang had Jing Xiang, Yan had Ma Yu, Hua had Li Juchuan, and Jingnan had Zheng Zhun,
units.literal: At that time Liang had Jing Xiang, Yan had Ma Yu, Hua Prefecture had Li Juchuan, and Jingnan had Zheng Zhun,

units.zh: 〈（《唐新纂》云：鄭準，士族，未第時，佐荊門上穀蓮幕，飛書走檄，不讓古人，秉直去邪，無慚往哲，考準為成汭書記，汭封上穀郡王。）〉
units.en: (New Tang Compendium: Zheng Zhun came from the gentry; before he passed the examinations he served on the lotus-staff of Shanggu at Jingmen, drafting dispatches that matched the ancients and upholding rectitude without shame before the sages of old. He served as secretary to Cheng Rui, who was enfeoffed as Prince of Shanggu.)〉
units.literal: (New Tang Compendium says: Zheng Zhun, of the gentry class, before passing the examinations assisted the Shanggu lotus-staff office at Jingmen; in flying letters and running proclamations he yielded to no ancients, upheld rectitude and expelled evil without shame before former sages. Examined: Zhun was secretary to Cheng Rui, and Rui was enfeoffed as Prince of Shanggu Commandery.)〉

units.zh: 自廣明大亂之後，諸侯割據方面，競延名士，以掌書檄。
units.en: After the great disorders of the Guangming reign, regional lords carved up the empire and competed to recruit famous scholars to draft their letters and battle proclamations.
units.literal: From after the great disorder of the Guangming era, feudal lords held regions by force and vied to summon famous scholars to manage letters and proclamations.

units.zh: 其父德諲事秦宗權，為申州刺史。
units.en: His father Zhao Dexin served Qin Zongquan and became prefect of Shen.
units.literal: His father Dexin served Qin Zongquan and was made prefect of Shen.

units.zh: 宗權反，德諲攻下襄陽。
units.en: When Zongquan turned rebel, Dexin took Xiangyang.
units.literal: When Zongquan rebelled, Dexin captured Xiangyang.

units.zh: 會其兵以攻蔡州，破之，德諲功多。
units.en: Dexin marched with him on Cai and helped break the city. His merit stood high.
units.literal: He then joined his troops to attack Cai Prefecture and broke it; Dexin’s merit was great.

units.zh: 德諲卒，子匡凝自立。
units.en: Dexin died, and Kuangning seized power for himself.
units.literal: When Dexin died, his son Kuangning installed himself.

units.zh: 是時，成汭死，雷彥恭襲取荊南，匡凝遣其弟匡明逐彥恭，太祖表匡凝荊襄節度使，以匡明為荊南留後。
units.en: Cheng Ru was dead and Lei Yan’gong had taken Jingnan. Kuangning sent his brother Kuangming to expel him. Zhu Wen made Kuangning commissioner of Jing-Xiang and Kuangming acting governor of Jingnan.
units.literal: At that time Cheng Ru had died and Lei Yan’gong had seized Jingnan. Kuangning sent his younger brother Kuangming to drive out Yan’gong. Taizu memorialized Kuangning as military commissioner of Jing-Xiang and made Kuangming acting governor of Jingnan.

units.zh: 梁太祖初鎮宣武，嘗為宗權所困，聞德諲降，大喜，表為行營副都統，河陽、保義、義昌三節度行軍司馬。
units.en: Zhu Wen, newly made lord of Xuanyi, had once been cornered by Zongquan. Dexin’s surrender delighted him. He made Dexin deputy supreme commander of the field army and liaison commissioner for Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang.
units.literal: When Taizu first held Xuanyi, he had once been trapped by Zongquan; hearing of Dexin’s surrender, he rejoiced greatly and memorialized him as deputy supreme commander of the field army and military affairs commissioner for the three circuits of Heyang, Baoyi, and Yichang.

units.zh: 梁太祖攻蔡州，宗權屢敗，德諲乃以山南東道七州降。
units.en: Zhu Wen attacked Cai again and again until Zongquan broke. Dexin then surrendered all seven prefectures of Shannan East.
units.literal: When Liang Taizu attacked Cai Prefecture, Zongquan was repeatedly defeated; Dexin thereupon surrendered the seven prefectures of Shannan East Circuit.

units.zh: 是則荀鶴之受知於梁祖舊矣，不待田頵之箋問而始被遇也。）〉
units.en: So the Liang Founder had known Xunhe long before Tian Yun's letter brought him to court.)〉
units.literal: Thus Xunhe had long won the Liang Founder's notice and did not await Tian Yun's letter of inquiry before first being received.)〉

units.zh: 頵將起兵，乃陰令以箋問至，太祖遇之頗厚。
units.en: When Yun prepared to rebel he secretly sent a letter of inquiry ahead; the Founder treated Xunhe very well.
units.literal: When Yun was about to raise troops he secretly sent a letter of inquiry; the Founder received him quite generously.

units.zh: 時田頵在宣州，甚重之。
units.en: Tian Yun was then at Xuanzhou and held him in high esteem.
units.literal: At that time Tian Yun was at Xuanzhou and valued him greatly.

units.zh: 及頵遇禍，太祖以其才表之，尋授翰林學士、主客員外郎。
units.en: After Yun's fall the Founder praised his talent at court and soon made him Hanlin academician and supernumerary vice director of the Ministry of Reception.
units.literal: When Yun met disaster the Founder memorialized on his talent and soon made him Hanlin academician and Supernumerary Vice Director in the Ministry of Reception for Dependencies.

units.zh: 三年，彥恭奔于楊行密，馬殷擒其弟彥雄等七人送于梁，斬于汴市，彥恭卒於淮南，澧、朗遂入于楚。
units.en: In year 3 Yan Gong fled to Yang Xingmi. Ma Yin seized his brother Yan Xiong and six others, sent the seven captives to Liang, and had them beheaded in Bian. Yan Gong died in Huainan. Li and Lang passed to Chu.
units.literal: In the third year Yan Gong fled to Yang Xingmi. Ma Yin captured his younger brother Yan Xiong and others—seven men in all—sent them to Liang, and had them executed in the Bian market. Yan Gong died in Huainan, and Li and Lang thereafter fell to Chu.

units.zh: 戊辰，遣使祭故淮南節度使楊行密、故升府節度使徐溫等墓。
units.en: On wuchen envoys were sent to offer sacrifice at the tombs of the former Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi, the former Shengfu military governor Xu Wen, and others.
units.literal: On wuchen envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifice at the tombs of the former Huainan military governor Yang Xingmi, the former Shengfu military governor Xu Wen, and others.

units.zh: 時都虞候朱友恭羽書聞於太祖，誣友裕按兵不追賊，太祖大怒，因驛騎傳符，令裨將龐師古代友裕為帥，仍令按劾其事。
units.en: Chief Commandant Zhu You Gong reported that You Yu had held his men back; the Founder, furious, sent Pang Shigu by relay to replace him and investigate.
units.literal: At the time Chief Commandant Zhu You Gong's urgent dispatch reached the Founder, falsely accusing You Yu of holding troops and not pursuing bandits; the Founder was greatly angry, and through post-horse transmitted tally, ordered deputy general Pang Shigu to replace You Yu as commander, still ordering investigation of the affair.

units.zh: 景福元年，總大軍伐徐。
units.en: In Jingfu 1 he led the main force against Xu.
units.literal: Jingfu year 1, commanded the great army to attack Xu.

units.zh: 廣明初，黃巢陷長安，遂投跡於太祖，洎居門下，未嘗一日不在左右。
units.en: When Huang Chao seized Chang'an in the first year of Guangming, Tong entered the Founder's service and from that day was never far from his side.
units.literal: Early Guangming, Huang Chao took Chang'an; he then cast his lot with the Founder, and once under his gate never a day was absent from his side.

units.zh: 太祖受禪，授左龍虎統軍兼元從新軍馬步都虞候。
units.en: When the Founder took the throne he made Han commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Guard and chief adjutant of his personal new army, horse and foot.
units.literal: The Founder received the abdication and appointed him commander of the Left Dragon-Tiger Guard and concurrently chief military adjutant of the original-following new army, horse and foot.

units.zh: 及太祖據同州，遂署右職。
units.en: Once the Founder held Tongzhou, he gave Tong a chief post on his staff.
units.literal: When the Founder held Tong Prefecture, he then appointed him to a right-hand post.

units.zh: 今將軍勇冠三軍，力戰於外，而孟楷專務壅蔽，奏章不達，下為庸才所製，無獨斷之明，破亡之兆必矣。
units.en: You fight abroad with unmatched courage while Meng Kai chokes every letter to court; mediocrities below him run the show, and without firm command ruin is certain.
units.literal: Now the general's courage crowns the three armies, fighting hard abroad, yet Meng Kai devotes himself to blocking; memorials do not arrive, below he is constrained by mediocrities and lacks the clarity of sole decision—the omen of ruin is sure.

units.zh: 時安陽公主初卒於魏，太祖乃遺嗣勳率長直官千人，實兵仗於橐中，肩舁以入於魏，聲言來致祭會葬，牙軍不之覺。
units.en: Princess Anyang had just died at Wei; the Founder sent Sixun with a thousand hand-picked men, weapons hidden in coffers carried on poles into the city under cover of funeral rites, and the guard army never suspected.
units.literal: At the time Princess Anyang had just died in Wei; the Founder then sent Sixun leading a thousand long-guard officers, with weapons packed in chests and borne on shoulders into Wei, declaring they came to offer sacrifice at the funeral—the guard army did not notice.

units.zh: 唐中和四年夏，太祖以朱珍為淄州刺史，令收兵於淄、青間，命捍監其兵，路逢大敵，皆破之。
units.en: Summer of Zhonghe 4, the Founder sent Zhu Zhen to gather troops between Zi and Qing with Han overseeing his force; every major foe they met was defeated.
units.literal: Summer, Tang Zhonghe year 4, the Founder made Zhu Zhen prefect of Zi and ordered him to gather troops between Zi and Qing; he ordered Han to supervise his troops; on the road they met great enemies and all were broken.

units.zh: 開平元年，拜右武衛上將軍。
units.en: In the first year of Kaiping he was made General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard.
units.literal: Kaiping year 1, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guard.

units.zh: 翌日，遂定策，戮偽監軍使，悉眾歸順於河中。
units.en: Next day the plan was fixed: the false inspector was killed, and the whole army went over to Hezhong.
units.literal: The next day he settled strategy, killed the false army supervisor, and with all his host submitted to Hezhong.

units.zh: 太祖曰：「我意素決，爾又如是，復何疑哉！」
units.en: The Founder replied, "My mind was made long ago; hearing you say the same, what doubt could remain?"
units.literal: The Founder said: "My mind was long settled; you speak thus too—what doubt remains!"

units.zh: 太祖每言曰：「敬翔、劉捏、寇彥卿，蓋為我而生。」
units.en: The Founder would say: "Jing Xiang, Liu Han, and Kou Yanqing might as well have been made for me."
units.literal: The Founder often said: "Jing Xiang, Liu Han, and Kou Yanqing were surely born for me."

units.zh: 太祖有所乘烏馬，號「一丈烏」，嘗以賜彥卿。
units.en: The Founder once gave him his black charger, the "Ten-foot Crow."
units.literal: The Founder had a black horse he rode called "One Zhang Crow"; he once bestowed it on Yanqing.

units.zh: 捍少為牙職，太祖初鎮夷門，以捍聰敏，擢副典客。
units.en: As a youth Han served in the yamen staff; when the Founder first took Bian he made the quick-witted Han his deputy master of ceremonies.
units.literal: Han in youth was a yamen staffer; when the Founder first held Yimen he because Han was clever promoted him deputy master of ceremonies.

units.zh: 太祖鎮汴，以彥卿將家子，擢在左右。
units.en: When the Founder governed Bian he kept Yanqing, a general's son, at his side.
units.literal: When the Founder held Bian he, because Yanqing was a general's son, promoted him to his side.

units.zh: 其年秋，太祖與河中交戰，再不利，連上章請兵於巢，偽右軍都尉孟楷抑而不進。
units.en: That autumn, twice beaten fighting Hezhong, the Founder pleaded again and again to Chao for reinforcements, but the rebel Right Army commissioner Meng Kai blocked every dispatch.
units.literal: That autumn the Founder fought Hezhong and twice met ill fortune; repeatedly he sent memorials asking troops of Chao, but the false Right Army commissioner Meng Kai suppressed them and they did not advance.

units.zh: 瞳揣太祖有擇福意，乃進說曰：「黃家以數十萬之師，值唐朝久安，人不習戰，因利乘便，遂下兩京。
units.en: Reading the Founder's wish to change sides, Tong urged him: "Huang's army of hundreds of thousands took both capitals only because the Tang had grown soft in long peace and men had forgotten war.
units.literal: Tong gauged that the Founder intended to choose fortune, and thereupon advanced counsel, saying: "The Huang house with an army of hundreds of thousands, encountering the Tang's long peace and men unpractised in war, rode advantage and seized both capitals.

units.zh: 秋罷，詣蜀行在，太祖遣人迎之。
units.en: When autumn brought his term to an end, he went to the imperial camp in Shu, and the Founder sent escorts to meet him.
units.literal: Autumn dismissed, he went to the Shu traveling court; the Founder sent men to welcome him.

units.zh: 龍紀二年，至東京，勞徠彌厚，賜第墅各一區，錢千緡，表為亳州團練使兼太清宮副使，加檢校工部尚書。
units.en: In Longji 2 he reached the Eastern Capital; the Founder received him with exceptional honors—a mansion, a country villa, a thousand strings of cash—and memorialized him Bozhou regimental commissioner and deputy head of the Grand Pure Palace, with acting rank as Minister of Works.
units.literal: Longji year 2, he reached the Eastern Capital; rewards and comfort were thicker still, granted one ward each of mansion and villa, a thousand strings of cash, memorialized as Bozhou regimental commissioner and vice-director of the Grand Pure Palace, added acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 是年冬，太祖征淮南，過郡，因求侍府幕，表為宣義軍節度副使，充兩使留後。
units.en: That winter, as the Founder marched on Huainan and passed through his circuit, Tong asked to join his staff and was made vice-commissioner of the Xuanyi army and regent for both civil and military commissioners.
units.literal: That winter the Founder campaigned against Huainan, passed through his prefecture; he therefore asked to serve in the commandery staff, was memorialized as vice-commissioner of the Xuanyi army and acting regent for both commissioners.

units.zh: 韓建傳判官司鄴昭宗之幸鳳翔也，太祖引兵入關，前鋒至左馮翊，鄴持印鑰迎謁道左。
units.en: Maye had served as Han Jian's administrative officer; when Zhaozong fled to Fengxiang and the Founder entered the Pass, Maye met the vanguard at Fengyi with seal and keys in hand.
units.literal: Si Maye had been Han Jian's administrative officer; when Zhaozong went to Fengxiang the Founder led troops into the Pass, the vanguard reaching Left Fengyi; Maye holding seal and keys welcomed him by the roadside.

units.zh: 太祖以兵圍華州，命入城招諭韓建，建果出降。
units.en: The Founder besieged Hua and sent Maye into the city to parley with Han Jian, who promptly surrendered.
units.literal: The Founder with troops besieged Hua Prefecture, ordered him into the city to summon and persuade Han Jian; Jian indeed came out and surrendered.

units.zh: 又使於金州，說其帥馮行襲，俾堅攀附。
units.en: He was also sent to Jinzhou to bind Feng Xingxi firmly to the Founder's cause.
units.literal: Again he was sent to Jin Prefecture to persuade its commander Feng Xingxi to hold fast to attachment.

units.zh: 文德元年十一月，蔡將申叢折宗權足，納款於太祖，使捍奏其事，加兼御史大夫。
units.en: In the eleventh month of Wende 1 the Cai general Shen Cong broke Zongquan's foot and surrendered; Han carried word of it to the Founder and received concurrent rank as Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: Wende year 1, eleventh month, the Cai general Shen Cong broke Zongquan's foot, submitted to the Founder; he had Han report the affair and added him concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 光化三年六月，太祖北伐鎮、定，至常山，而王钅容危懾，送款於太祖，命捍入壁門傳諭。
units.en: In the sixth month of Guanghua 3 the Founder marched north against Zhen and Ding; at Changshan a terrified Wang Rong submitted, and the Founder sent Han through the barbican to announce terms.
units.literal: Guanghua year 3, sixth month, the Founder north campaigned against Zhen and Ding, reaching Changshan; Wang Rong in peril and fear sent submission to the Founder, and ordered Han to enter the barbican gate to proclaim the message.

units.zh: 太祖迎昭宗於岐下，以捍為親軍指揮。
units.en: When the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Qi's walls, he made Han commander of his personal guard.
units.literal: The Founder welcomed Zhaozong below Qi and made Han commander of the personal army.

units.zh: 天復三年正月，宋文通令客將郭啟奇使於太祖，命捍復命。
units.en: In the first month of Tianfu 3, Song Wentong sent his guest-officer Guo Qiqi to the Founder with Han as the envoy to reply.
units.literal: Tianfu year 3, first month, Song Wentong ordered the guest-officer Guo Qiqi as envoy to the Founder and ordered Han to answer the mission.

units.zh: 四月，太祖伐王師範於青州，改左右長直都指揮使。
units.en: In the fourth month, as the Founder attacked Wang Shifan at Qingzhou, Han was made commander of the left and right Long-Straight guards.
units.literal: Fourth month, the Founder campaigned against Wang Shifan at Qingzhou and changed him to commander of the left and right Long-Straight commands.

units.zh: 及上黨纏兵，太祖親往巡撫，以捍為御營使。
units.en: When war tangled at Shangdang the Founder went in person and made Han commissioner of the imperial camp.
units.literal: When Shangdang tangled troops, the Founder in person went to oversee; he made Han imperial-camp commissioner.

units.zh: 大軍次昂車，斥候來告蕃戎逼澤州，命捍以兵千人赴之，並軍遂遁，車駕還京，授捍侍衛親軍都指揮使。
units.en: The army halted at Angche; scouts reported barbarians pressing Ze; the Founder sent Han with a thousand men and the enemy fled; when the emperor returned to the capital Han was made commander of the palace guard.
units.literal: The great army halted at Angche; scouts came reporting barbarians pressing Ze Prefecture; he ordered Han with a thousand troops to go; the combined armies thereupon fled; the imperial carriage returned to the capital and Han was granted commander of the personal guard of the palace guards.

units.zh: 雖無決戰爭鋒之績，而承命奔走，數揚命令，勤幹涖職，以至崇顯焉。
units.en: He won no great battle, yet by racing on every order, bearing the Founder's word again and again, and tireless service he rose to the highest honors.
units.literal: Though he had no achievement of decisive battle and contending edge, yet receiving orders he ran and hastened, repeatedly proclaimed commands, diligently carried office—and so reached eminent display.

units.zh: 及淮人不恭，太祖屢以軍南渡，路由州境，敬蕘悉心供億，太祖甚嘉之。
