units.en: Each time the Founder crossed the Huai with an army and passed through Ying, Jinrao supplied his needs without stint, and the Founder took great notice.
units.literal: When Huainan men were not respectful, the Founder repeatedly with armies crossed south, the route passing through his prefectural borders; Jinrao with whole heart supplied provisions; the Founder greatly praised him.

units.zh: 雖非太祖舊臣，而遠輸懇款，保境合兵，以輔興王之運，有足稱者。
units.en: He was no veteran of the Founder's camp, yet from afar he offered loyal service, held his territory, and marshaled troops to help the new dynasty—grounds enough for praise.
units.literal: Though not an old minister of the Founder, yet from afar he conveyed earnest pledge, preserved borders and united troops, to assist the fortune of the rising king—there is enough to praise.

units.zh: 太祖以客禮遇之，尋表為亳州團練副使，知州事。
units.en: The Founder received him as an honored guest and soon made him vice-regimental commissioner at Bozhou with charge of the prefecture.
units.literal: The Founder treated him with guest rites; soon memorialized him as Bozhou regimental vice-commissioner and acting prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 唐昭宗之鳳翔，太祖迎奉未出，劭有疑謀，遂令赴華州，詣丞相府以議其事；
units.en: When Zhaozong fled to Fengxiang and the Founder had not yet marched to receive him, Shao's plotting aroused suspicion; he was sent to Hua to consult the chief minister's office—
units.literal: Tang Emperor Zhaozong went to Fengxiang; the Founder had not yet gone out to welcome him; Shao had doubtful schemes; he was then ordered to go to Hua Prefecture, to approach the chief minister's office to deliberate the affair;

units.zh: 唐景福元年三月，太祖以壽州刺史江儒反下蔡鎮使，李立率兵攻濠梁，刺史張遂俾嗣勳持州印籍戶口以歸於太祖。
units.en: In the third month of Jingfu 1, when Shou prefect Jiang Ru rebelled at Xia'ai, Li Li attacked Hao and Liang; prefect Zhang Sui sent Sixun with the seal and household registers to submit to the Founder.
units.literal: Tang Jingfu year 1, third month, the Founder because Shou prefect Jiang Ru rebelled [at] Xia'ai garrison commander Li Li led troops attacking Hao and Liang; prefect Zhang Sui had Sixun hold the prefectural seal and register households to return submission to the Founder.

units.zh: 乾寧二年三月，楊行密復攻濠州，張遂遣嗣勳求援於太祖。
units.en: In the third month of Qianning 2, when Yang Xingmi attacked Haozhou again, Zhang Sui sent Sixun to plead for help.
units.literal: Qianning year 2, third month, Yang Xingmi again attacked Hao Prefecture; Zhang Sui sent Sixun to beg aid from the Founder.

units.zh: 俄而郡陷，嗣勳無所歸，即署為元從押牙、副典客，頗稱任使。
units.en: When the city soon fell Sixun had nowhere to go; the Founder made him yamen adjutant of his personal following and deputy master of ceremonies, and found him thoroughly reliable.
units.literal: Soon the prefecture fell; Sixun had nowhere to return; he was at once appointed original-following yamen adjutant and deputy master of ceremonies, quite fit for employment and missions.

units.zh: 天復中，太祖迎昭宗於岐下，軍至華之西，使嗣勳入見，韓建即時同出迎謁。
units.en: During Tianfu, as the Founder brought Zhaozong from Qixia and halted west of Hua, he sent Sixun in to audience; Han Jian came out at once to greet them together.
units.literal: In Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Qixia and the army reached west of Hua, he sent Sixun in to see him; Han Jian at once came out together to welcome and pay court.

units.zh: 及羅紹威將殺牙軍，遣使告於太祖，求為外援。
units.en: When Luo Shaowei planned to destroy the guard corps, he asked the Founder for reinforcements.
units.literal: When Luo Shaowei was about to kill the guard army, he sent envoys to inform the Founder and beg for outside aid.

units.zh: 唐中和中，從太祖赴汴，以其折節，頗見親昵，首為右騎都將。
units.en: In Zhonghe of Tang he followed the Founder to Bian; his discipline won favor, and he became the first Right Cavalry commander.
units.literal: In Tang Zhonghe he followed the Founder to Bian; because of his self-restraint he was quite treated with intimacy, and first became Right Cavalry commander.

units.zh: 光啟中，李罕之會晉軍圍張宗奭於盟津，太祖遣丁會、葛從周、存敬同往馳救。
units.en: In Guangqi, Li Hanzhi and the Jin besieged Zhang Zongshi at Mengjin; the Founder sent Ding Hui, Ge Congzhou, and Cunjin to relieve him.
units.literal: In Guangqi, Li Hanzhi joined Jin troops in besieging Zhang Zongshi at Meng Ford; the Founder sent Ding Hui, Ge Congzhou, and Cunjing together to gallop to the rescue.

units.zh: 太祖東征徐、兗，存敬屢有俘斬之功。
units.en: In the eastern campaigns against Xu and Yan, Cunjin took many prisoners and heads.
units.literal: When the Founder campaigned east against Xu and Yan, Cunjing repeatedly had merit in captures and beheadings.

units.zh: 凡受指顧，皆與機會，矢石所及，必以身先，太祖屢加優異，以為行營都指揮使、檢校右僕射。
units.en: He seized every chance in battle and always led where stones and arrows fell; the Founder favored him and made him field commander and Acting Right Vice Director.
units.literal: Whenever he received orders he always seized the moment; wherever arrows and stones reached he must take the lead; the Founder repeatedly showed him special favor and made him field army overall commander and Acting Right Vice Director.

units.zh: 天復元年春，太祖以河中節度使王珂與太原結親，憑恃驕恣，命存敬統大軍討之。
units.en: In spring of Tianfu 1 the Founder, angered that Wang Ke of Hezhong had married into Taiyuan and grown insolent, sent Cunjin with a great army against him.
units.literal: Tianfu 1 spring, the Founder because Hezhong military commissioner Wang Ke had allied with Taiyuan and relied on arrogance and license ordered Cunjing to command the great army to punish him.

units.zh: 太祖嘉之，乃以存敬為護國軍留後。
units.en: The Founder was pleased and made Cunjin acting commissioner of Huguo.
units.literal: The Founder praised this and thereupon made Cunjing Huguo army acting commissioner.

units.zh: 太祖聞之，痛惜移晷。
units.en: The Founder mourned him for hours on hearing the news.
units.literal: When the Founder heard it he grieved and regretted for a watch.

units.zh: 太祖為元帥，補元帥府押牙，充四鎮通讚官行首兼右長直都指揮使，累奏授檢校司徒，領洺州刺史。
units.en: As grand marshal the Founder made him headquarters guard officer, chief protocol officer of the four commands and Right Long Direct commander, and had him memorialized Acting Minister of Works and prefect of Mingzhou.
units.literal: When the Founder was grand marshal he supplemented him as the marshal's headquarters guard officer, served as head of the four commands communications officers and concurrently Right Long Direct overall commander, and repeatedly memorialized to appoint Acting Minister of Works and grant Ming prefecture.

units.zh: 羅紹威將殺牙軍，遣使告於太祖，太祖命彥卿使於魏，密與紹威謀之。
units.en: When Luo Shaowei moved against the guard corps he asked the Founder for help; the Founder sent Yanqing to Wei to conspire with him.
units.literal: When Luo Shaowei was about to kill the guard army he sent envoys to inform the Founder; the Founder ordered Yanqing as envoy to Wei to plot secretly with Shaowei.

units.zh: 善騎射，好書史，復善伺太祖之旨，凡所作為，動皆云合。
units.en: He excelled at riding and archery, loved history, and read the Founder's mind so well that his every act seemed foreordained.
units.literal: Skilled in mounted archery, fond of books and histories, and again skilled at reading the Founder's intent—whatever he did always matched like clouds joining.

units.zh: 天復中，太祖迎昭宗於鳳翔，累與岐軍對陣。
units.en: During Tianfu, as the Founder brought Zhaozong from Fengxiang, he fought the Qi army again and again.
units.literal: In Tianfu, when the Founder welcomed Zhaozong at Fengxiang, he repeatedly faced Qi troops in array.

units.zh: 嘗躬擐甲胄，乘其所賜烏馬，馳騁於陣前，太祖目之曰：「真神王也！」
units.en: Once, armored and mounted on his gifted black horse, he charged before the ranks; the Founder watched and cried, "A true war god!"
units.literal: He once personally donned armor and helmet, rode the black horse bestowed on him, and galloped before the lines; the Founder eyed him and said: "Truly a spirit king!"

units.zh: 《九國誌·朱景傳》：梁祖聞景名，命寇彥卿率勁騎三千襲霍丘，圖取景，且諭梁祖之意令降，景率其徒戰於丘墟林澤中，射死者無數，彥卿兵折力殫而去。）〉
units.en: The 《Nine States Chronicle · Biography of Zhu Jing》 says the Liang Founder sent Yanqing with three thousand elite cavalry to take Huoqiu and capture Jing, offering surrender terms; Jing fought him in scrub and marsh, killing many; Yanqing withdrew with his force spent.）〉
units.literal: The 《Chronicle of the Nine States · Biography of Zhu Jing》: The Liang Founder heard Jing's fame and ordered Kou Yanqing to lead three thousand crack horsemen to raid Huoqiu, intending to capture Jing, and also conveyed the Liang Founder's intent that he submit; Jing led his followers to fight in ruined mounds and forest marsh; those shot dead were countless; Yanqing's troops were broken and strength exhausted and departed.）〉

units.zh: 杜荀鶴，池州人。
units.en: Du Xunhe came from Chizhou.
units.literal: Du Xunhe, a man of Chizhou.

units.zh: 〈（辛文房《唐才子傳》：荀鶴，字彥之，牧之微子也。）〉
units.en: (Xin Wenfang's 《Records of Tang Talents》 says Xunhe, styled Yanzhi, was an illegitimate son of Du Mu.)〉
units.literal: (Xin Wenfang's 《Records of Tang Talents》: Xunhe, style Yanzhi, was a minor son of Muzhi.)〉

units.zh: 善為詩，辭句切理，為時所許。
units.en: He wrote poetry with phrases that cut to the point and won contemporary praise.
units.literal: Skilled at poetry, his phrases cut to reason, approved by the age.

units.zh: 大順二年，裴贄侍郎放第八人登科，正月十日放榜，正荀鶴生朝也。
units.en: In Dashun 2 Vice Minister Pei Zan placed him eighth on the list; the roster was posted on the tenth day of the first month—Xunhe's own birthday.
units.literal: In Dazhun year 2 Vice Minister Pei Zan released the eighth man on the rolls; on the tenth day of the first month the list was posted—exactly Xunhe's birthday.

units.zh: 苞蓄未及泄丁重疾，旬日而卒。
units.en: His grudges had not yet been acted on when he fell gravely ill and died within ten days.
units.literal: His hoarded spite had not yet been vented when he fell gravely ill and died within ten days.

units.zh: 既而恃太祖之勢，凡搢紳間己所不悅者，日屈指怒數，將謀盡殺之。
units.en: Soon, trusting in the Founder's favor, he daily counted on his fingers the courtiers he hated and plotted to kill them all.
units.literal: Before long, relying on the Founder's power, among the gentry anyone he disliked he would daily count on his fingers in anger, plotting to kill them all.

units.zh: 又，《唐新纂》云：荀鶴舉進士及第，東歸，過夷門，獻梁太祖詩句云：「四海九州空第一，不同諸鎮府封王。」
units.en: The 《Tang New Compilation》 adds: Xunhe took his jinshi degree, went east, passed Yimen, and gave the Liang Founder this verse: "First in all the realm—unlike the warlords made kings of their circuits."
units.literal: Further, the 《Tang New Compilation》 says: Xunhe passed the jinshi examination, returned east, passed Yimen, and presented lines to the Liang Founder: "Alone first through the four seas and nine provinces—unlike the various governors enfeoffed as kings."

units.zh: 〈（《唐才子傳》：荀鶴嘗謁梁王朱全忠，與之坐，忽無雲而雨，王以為天泣不祥，命作詩，稱意，王喜之。
units.en: (The 《Records of Tang Talents》 records that Xunhe once visited Prince of Liang Zhu Quanzhong; as they sat together rain fell though the sky was clear; the prince took it as heaven weeping and ordered a poem; pleased with it, he was delighted.
units.literal: (The 《Records of Tang Talents》 says: Xunhe once called on Prince of Liang Zhu Quanzhong and sat with him; suddenly rain fell from a cloudless sky; the prince thought heaven wept—an ill omen—and ordered him to compose a poem; it pleased him and the prince was delighted.

units.zh: 荀鶴寒進，連敗文場，甚苦，至是送春官。
units.en: Xunhe had come up in poverty, failed again and again in the examinations, and suffered greatly before he was finally sent to the Ministry of Rites.
units.literal: Xunhe came up poor, failed repeatedly in the literary arena, suffered greatly, and only then was sent to the spring office.

units.zh: 鍾傳，洪州高安人也。
units.en: Zhong Chuan came from Gao’an in Hong Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhong Chuan was a native of Gao’an in Hong Prefecture.

units.zh: 傳以州兵擊賊，頻勝，遂逐觀察使，自稱留後。
units.en: Chuan beat the bandits again and again with prefectural troops, drove out the observation commissioner, and called himself acting governor.
units.literal: Chuan with prefectural troops attacked bandits and won repeatedly; he thereupon drove out the observation commissioner and styled himself acting military governor.

units.zh: 傳居江西三十餘年，累拜太保、中書令，封南平王。
units.en: Chuan held Jiangxi for more than thirty years, rose to Grand Guardian and Secretariat Director, and was made Prince of Nanping.
units.literal: Chuan dwelt in Jiangxi more than thirty years, was repeatedly promoted to Grand Guardian and Secretariat Director, and enfeoffed Prince of Nanping.

units.zh: 唐以洪州為鎮南軍，拜傳節度使。
units.en: Tang made Hong the Pacify-the-South circuit and named Chuan its commissioner.
units.literal: Tang made Hong Prefecture the Pacify-the-South circuit and appointed Chuan military commissioner.

units.zh: 事州為小校，黃巢攻掠江淮，所在盜起，往往據州縣。
units.en: He was a petty officer of the prefecture. Huang Chao ravaged the Jiang-Huai; in his wake rebels seized town after town.
units.literal: He served the prefecture as a junior officer. Huang Chao swept the Jiang-Huai region; wherever he passed, bandits rose and often seized prefectures and counties.

units.zh: 全諷聞之，明日乃亦聽命，請以女妻傳子匡時。
units.en: Quanfeng heard the prayer. The next day he submitted and offered his daughter to Chuan’s son Kuangshi.
units.literal: When Quanfeng heard this, the next day he too submitted and asked to give his daughter in marriage to Chuan’s son Kuangshi.

units.zh: 天祐三年，傳卒，子匡時自稱留後，請命於唐。
units.en: In Tianyou 3 (906) Chuan died. His son Kuangshi called himself acting governor and bowed to Tang.
units.literal: In the third year of Tianyou, Chuan died; his son Kuangshi styled himself acting military governor and submitted to Tang.

units.zh: 已而傳養子延規與匡時爭立，乞兵於楊渥，渥遣秦裴等攻匡時，匡時敗，被執歸廣陵。
units.en: Soon Chuan’s adopted son Yangui fought Kuangshi for power and called on Yang Wo. Wo sent Qin Pei and others against Kuangshi, broke him, and carried him off to Guangling.
units.literal: Before long Chuan’s adopted son Yangui contended with Kuangshi for rule and begged troops from Yang Wo; Wo sent Qin Pei and others to attack Kuangshi. Kuangshi was defeated, seized, and taken to Guangling.

units.zh: 是時，危全諷、韓師德等分據撫、吉諸州，傳皆不能節度，以兵攻之，稍聽命，獨全諷不能下，乃自率兵圍之。
units.en: Wei Quanfeng, Han Shide, and others held Fu and Ji. Chuan could not rule them from afar; he marched on them until most bent the knee. Only Quanfeng held out, so Chuan went in person to besiege him.
units.literal: At that time Wei Quanfeng, Han Shide, and others each held Fu and Ji prefectures. Chuan could not command them; he attacked with troops and they gradually submitted—only Quanfeng could not be brought down, and he therefore led troops himself to besiege him.

units.zh: 城中夜火起，諸將請急攻之，傳曰：「吾聞君子不迫人之危。」
units.en: Night fires flared inside the walls. His generals begged to storm the city. Chuan said: “A gentleman does not kick a man when he is down.”
units.literal: Fire broke out in the city by night. The generals asked for an urgent assault. Chuan said: “I have heard that a gentleman does not press a man in peril.”

units.zh: 乃掃地祭天，向城再拜，祝曰：「全諷不降，非民之罪，願天止火。」
units.en: He swept clean ground, offered to Heaven, bowed twice toward the walls, and prayed: “If Quanfeng will not yield, the fault is not the people’s. Let the fire die.”
units.literal: He swept the ground and sacrificed to Heaven, bowed twice toward the city, and prayed: “If Quanfeng will not submit, it is not the people’s crime—may Heaven halt the fire.”

units.zh: 江夏伶人杜洪者，亦據鄂州，楊行密屢攻之，洪頗倚傳為首尾。
units.en: Du Hong, a Jiangxia player turned warlord, held Ezhou. Yang Xingmi struck him again and again, and Hong counted on Chuan to guard his back.
units.literal: Du Hong, a Jiangxia actor, also held Ezhou. Yang Xingmi attacked him many times; Hong leaned heavily on Chuan as his rear support.

units.zh: 荊南高季昌進瑞橘數十顆，質狀百味，倍勝常貢。
units.en: Gao Jichang of Jingnan sent dozens of auspicious oranges, finer in taste and look than ordinary tribute by far.
units.literal: Gao Jichang of Jingnan presented several tens of auspicious oranges, their quality and form a hundredfold better than ordinary tribute.

units.zh: 且橘當冬熟，今方仲夏，時人咸異其事，因稱為瑞。
units.en: Oranges ripen in winter, yet it was midsummer—men took it for a miracle and called them auspicious.
units.literal: Oranges should ripen in winter; now it was midsummer—people of the time all marveled at the matter and therefore called them auspicious.

units.zh: 五月，以唐朝宰臣張文蔚、楊涉並為門下侍郎、平章事；
units.en: In the fifth month former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
units.literal: In the fifth month, former Tang chief ministers Zhang Wenwei and Yang She were both made Vice Directors of the Secretariat and Grand Councilors;
